News.title: Man, 50, charged with arson after ‘starting 10 fires’ at popular park in early hours during heatwave
News.content:
PARK BLAZE Man, 50, charged with arson after ‘starting 10 fires’ at popular park in early hours during heatwave

A MAN has been charged with arson after allegedly starting ten fires at a popular park during a heatwave.

Isaac Shozi, 50, was arrested yesterday morning after the London Fire Brigade responded to reports of arson in London Fields, east London.

Shozi was taken into police custody on suspicion of arson, setting fires and possession of a Class A drug, and has since been charged.

Fire services quickly extinguished around ten fires within the park and thankfully no injuries have been reported.





Shozi is due to appear at Barkingside Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

Detective Superintendent Liz Cumber, who leads policing in central east London, said: “No one can be in any doubt about the dangers of starting fires, particularly following the recent hot weather and heightened risk of wildfires.

“Even small fires can spread quickly and put people, buildings and open spaces at risk.

“We take all reports of this nature extremely seriously and work closely with partners, including the London Fire Brigade.

“We will investigate all incidents, identify those responsible and ensure appropriate action is taken against those who are reported to have endangered the public.”

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “Anyone who witnesses a fire, or behaviour that could pose a risk of a fire starting, should call 999 immediately.

“Prompt reporting can help emergency services respond quickly and prevent fires from spreading and causing serious harm.”

This comes after millions of Brits were left fuming on Friday after a blaring emergency alert suddenly ripped through their phones, warning of the soaring risk of wildfires.



The government urged people to “not light anything that could spark a fire”, including barbecues, campfires and fireworks, as Britain battled another spell of scorching heat.

It warned: “Even a small flame can rapidly develop into a major wildfire placing lives, homes, businesses and emergency responders at risk.”

The alert added: “Recipients will also be urged to report any fire immediately by calling 999.”

On Thursday, 11 major fire incidents were reported in the West Midlands alone, with 19 homes completely destroyed and 18 others damaged as families were forced to evacuate.

But UK residents were left almost hysterical at the lack of severity of the alert.



One fumed: “The noise accompanying that emergency alert feels overkill.

“Lot of older people or those hiding phones for their safety possibly put at risk. Does it have to come with a loud noise?”

News.title: Moment riot cops drag snoozing suspect from rooftop after he ‘hurled tiles’ at officers during 48-hour stand-off
News.content:
THIS is the moment riot cops dragged a snoozing suspect from a rooftop following a 48-hour stand-off.

The suspect, 37, had reportedly hurled tiles at police during the lengthy incident at a property in Salford.



Footage shows the man dozing on top of a back porch roof, unaware that Tactical Aid Unit officers had gathered in the garden below him.

The cops, wearing helmets and other riot gear, gently placed a ladder against the ledge, with one officer climbing up and grabbing the man’s legs while he sleeps.





The man is startled and a struggle ensued as he tried to resist the cop by appearing to repeatedly punch him.

But the cop drags him down the ladder and onto the ground.



His trousers appear to fall down during the chaos and police pile on top of him to detain and arrest him.

Greater Manchester Police said the incident, which began on Thursday, was brought to a safe conclusion yesterday afternoon.

A spokesperson for the force said that the incident was in relation to an arrest attempt for the man from another police force.

The suspect, who was wanted on recall to prison for other matters, had previously been pictured wearing a Leonardo DiCaprio jumper and hurling tiles off the roof.



Police at the scene had tried to negotiate with him, but the man refused to come down.

Firefighters and paramedics were also called to the scene with a cordon put in place

Two police officers suffered minor injuries during the incident and the man remains in custody.

He has been arrested on suspicion of causing public nuisance, criminal damage, public order offences, burglary and assaulting two police officers.



Detective Chief Inspector Helen Bagnall, of our Salford District, said: “During two days of disruption to the local community, we worked continuously with our partners to bring this matter to a safe conclusion.

“This was an extensive use of vital policing resources and clearly demonstrates the dangers our officers face on a daily basis in order to protect the people of Greater Manchester.

“Two of our officers suffered minor injuries during this incident.

“I would like to reiterate my thanks to the people of Salford for their patience and understanding whilst emergency service personnel dealt with this incident.

“Some properties have been damaged as a result of this man’s actions. We will work with partners to ensure affected residents will be supported going forward.”

News.title: Brit girl, 12, who vanished in Japan found days later after going off by herself ‘to visit famous anime locations’
News.content:
HOLIDAY HUNT Brit girl, 12, who vanished in Japan found days later after going off by herself ‘to visit famous anime locations’

A 12-YEAR-OLD Brit girl has been found safe days after vanishing on a family holiday in Japan.

Carmelita Lakdesha Paul was located alive on Saturday night after she ventured away from her family to visit a famous anime location in Tokyo, officials say.



Officers spent days searching for her before she arrived alone and unharmed at a police phone box in Yokohama – 30 minutes south of Tokyo – at around 8pm on Saturday evening.

The teen told officers she had visited an anime location and spent time at internet cafe but eventually began to miss her parents, according to Japan Today.



Once located, she was taken into protective custody to be reunited with her family.

According to Japan News, Carmelita told police that she had stayed the night at internet cafes.

In Japan, internet cafes enforce strict age limits, barring anyone under the age of 18 to enter the premises past late-night hours.

This fact raises serious questions about how a 12-year-old was able to stay multiple nights.

While police haven’t revealed any other details, they say they do not believe any crime occurred.

Carmelita arrived in Japan for sightseeing with her parents and older brother on July 21.



Her family said they last saw her on August 12, at their Tokyo apartment but when they woke up the next morning she was gone.

The schoolgirl was spotted walking through Tokyo’s Kamata district on CCTV footage that morning.

She later boarded a train 20 minutes south to Yokohama Station, upon which police lost track of her whereabouts.

Carmelita did not take her phone or passport and her family said she had no more than around £70 with her.

Her father had spoken with her just the night before she went missing and said there was nothing suspicious about her behaviour.



Her disappearance came as record breaking rain battered Japans capital city with around 300,000 people forced to evacuate.

Torrential rain battered eastern Japan on Thursday, triggering horror flooding, landslides, power cuts and transport chaos as officials issued their highest-level heavy rain warning for the region for the first time.

News.title: Eritrean man, 33, raped pensioner outside church after dragging victim behind fences in vile 20-minute attack
News.content:
CHURCH HORROR Eritrean man, 33, raped pensioner outside church after dragging victim behind fences in vile 20-minute attack

A MAN has been found guilty of raping a pensioner outside a church.

Bruke Desalagne, 33, dragged a man in his 60s behind a fence at St John’s Church in Harrow, north London before carrying out the vile 20-minute-long attack.

At Harrow Crown Court, Desalagne, from Eritrea, pleaded guilty to raping the victim on July 23 last year and is due to be sentenced in Autumn.

At the time of the prolonged attack, police were called to Station Road following reports of a sexual assault.





A witness saw the incident from her car window while driving by and quickly phoned the police.

Cops rushed to the scene and Desalagne, of no fixed address, was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault and rape.

He claimed he was initially trying to help the elderly victim, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, because he was intoxicated.

In court, CCTV of the awful assault was played, which also showed traffic passing close to the scene.

Every time a member of the public walked by Desalagne would pause the attack, the jury heard.

Speaking about the grim CCTV footage, Simon Shannon, prosecuting, said: “You can see the defendant dragging the heavily intoxicated victim from the bench where he was sitting, and dragged him to the grass area.”

Bibi Ihuomah, defending, argued there was no evidence that the attack had involved rape.

But a guilty verdict was handed down to Desalagne who reportedly remained emotionless throughout the trial.



Det Con Luke Revill of the Metropolitan Police said: “Bruke Desalagne is a dangerous offender who targeted a defenceless, vulnerable, elderly man.

“Thanks to members of the public alerting the police, he was arrested at the scene, charged the following day and remanded by the courts.

“We are committed to bringing sexual predators like Desalagne to justice.

“We would urge anyone who has been the victim of similar offending to get in touch with the police.

“You will be supported and listened to by officers.”

News.title: One dead and 12 injured as tour group ‘thrown from horse-drawn carriage after brakes failed’ and smashed into tree
News.content:
CARRIAGE TRAGEDY One dead and 12 injured as tour group ‘thrown from horse-drawn carriage after brakes failed’ and smashed into tree

ONE person has been killed and 12 others injured in a major incident involving a horse-drawn carriage.

The tragedy happened in the Swiss canton of Graubünden on Saturday.

While going downhill, the driver noticed the brakes were no longer working properly.



According to police, he tried to steer the convoy – made up of one carriage and two trailers – onto a flatter section of road.



But disaster struck during the manoeuvre when one of the horses fell, sending the trailer careering out of control.

The carriage crashed into a tree at the side of the road, throwing several passengers from the vehicle.

A 73-year-old woman suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.



Twelve other passengers were injured and rushed to hospital by three helicopters and four ambulances.

A police investigation is now ongoing to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the incident.

This comes after a tourist in a horse-drawn carriage was thrown to his death in New York.

Romanch Mahajan, 18, was riding through Central Park with his parents and younger brother when the horse pulling them suddenly bolted, causing the cart to tip over.



The teen, on a family holiday from India, smashed his head on the ground as he was thrown from the cart as it collided with another coach.

He was rushed to the New York-Presbyterian Weill Cornell Medical Center but tragically passed away on Wednesday night.

Shocked onlooker Tatianna Bresler told the New York Post: “The horse got scared and ran super fast.”

The 20-year-old said she called 911 as soon as she saw the crash.

“The immediate reaction was just like ‘oh my god, oh my god my god’ like covering my eyes because I thought maybe someone had gotten smushed or something,” she said.



The seven-year-old horse, named as Sampson, was stopped in the park and was uninjured.

He had only been in the park for six weeks.
