In a renewed diplomatic effort to advance the stalled Gaza ceasefire, U.S. negotiator and President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner held a rare meeting with the Hamas chief on Sunday.

Kushner is slated to meet with Israel's prime minister on Monday in discussions aimed at saving a 15-point, U.S.-backed roadmap that requires Hamas to disarm in Gaza and Israel to pull back its forces from the war-torn Palestinian territory.

At stake is the survival of approximately 2 million people in Gaza and the rebuilding of the densely populated enclave, which remains mostly under the control of Israeli forces more than 10 months after the ceasefire halted major military operations. A meeting last year between Kushner, fellow envoy Steve Witkoff, and Hamas leaders in Egypt helped secure the original ceasefire, which has since stalled over the key requirement of Hamas’ disarmament.

Confirmation of the rare meeting in Egypt with Hamas' Khalil al-Hayya came from a regional official and a Hamas official, both speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to address reporters. Kushner belonged to a three-member envoy delegation meeting al-Hayya, alongside mediating officials from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey.

Netanyahu’s remarks last week cast more doubt on the deal to disarm Hamas ( Getty )

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly rejected the 15-point roadmap last week in a rare show of defiance toward the Trump administration, Israel’s chief ally.

Kushner, former British prime minister Tony Blair, and Nickolay Mladenov—director of the U.S.-established Board of Peace overseeing the ceasefire—are now scheduled to meet with Netanyahu on Monday, according to diplomatic and knowledgeable sources speaking on condition of anonymity.

Ahead of Monday's talks, several regional powers, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, issued a joint statement condemning Israel’s rejection of the plan, declaring that "Israel now bears responsibility for obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza." Other signatories included Jordan, Pakistan, Indonesia, and the ceasefire mediators.

The foreign ministers’ statement also called on the U.S. and the Board of Peace to execute "immediate and concrete measures" to stop any party from blocking the implementation of the plan.

The regional official noted that Kushner’s meeting with the Hamas leader was designed to guarantee the group’s adherence to the roadmap, particularly concerning disarmament, prior to his sitting down with Netanyahu.

A Hamas official stated that the group remains committed and is awaiting mediators to initiate the 14-day negotiation window to establish an implementation schedule. That phase requires all parties to approve the roadmap before starting.

The official added that the Hamas leader insisted Israel cease its attacks on Gaza and pull back to the poorly defined "yellow line" separating the territory before implementation begins. Israeli forces have advanced past that line and currently control around 60% of Gaza.

In May, Netanyahu expressed intentions to expand control to 70%, saying Israel was "tightening the grip" on Hamas "from every direction."

The White House referred questions regarding Kushner's discussions to the Board of Peace, which offered no immediate comment. The Tony Blair Institute also declined to comment.

Under the roadmap, Hamas would surrender weapons to a Palestinian technocratic committee designated to oversee daily administration in the enclave. The committee has not yet entered Gaza. However, Hamas has conditioned the surrender of its heaviest arms on the creation of a Palestinian state, a condition rejected by Israel’s government.

The roadmap outlines a gradual surrender of weapons by Hamas while Israeli forces halt attacks and begin withdrawing. Yet Netanyahu maintains Israel will not pull back from any position in Gaza until Hamas is totally disarmed.

This impasse leaves other components of the ceasefire, including reconstruction and the placement of international forces to divide Israeli troops from committee-governed areas, on hold.

Netanyahu faces a challenging Oct. 27 election as he attempts to retain power with a coalition featuring hardline ministers on Gaza policy. The political timeline also overlaps with the upcoming anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on southern Israel that triggered the war.

On Sunday, Netanyahu's Likud party answered the regional powers' statement by asserting that "Arab states want to topple" Netanyahu so centrist candidate Gadi Eisenkot and center-left leader Yair Golan "will give them everything they want. That will not happen."

Hundreds of migrants trying to reach the Spanish exclave of Ceuta by land and sea were arrested by Moroccan security forces, Moroccan state television reported Sunday, as authorities tightened security along the border following calls for a new mass crossing.

Moroccan state broadcaster Medi 1 TV said 294 migrants from sub-Saharan Africa were arrested Saturday while attempting to enter Ceuta. Authorities also arrested 61 Moroccans accused of facilitating the migration attempts, the broadcaster reported.

The attempted crossings followed a surge in social media posts calling on migrants to make their way to Ceuta, a Spanish city on Morocco’s northern coast. In response, Moroccan and Spanish authorities beefed up security presence and limited movement toward the area.

The latest attempt comes two weeks after tens of thousands of would-be migrants, driven by poverty and misinformation, rushed toward Ceuta in one of the deadliest migration crises to hit the region. At least 90 people died on both sides of the border, according to official numbers, while human rights groups reported higher figures.

The interior ministry did not respond to AP’s questions about the latest arrests or the number of security personnel deployed around the border to prevent a new migration push.

A senior Moroccan diplomat previously said that more than 20,000 Moroccan security personnel are deployed along the border with Ceuta each day, at a cost of hundreds of millions of dollars. The diplomat was not authorized to be publicly named speaking about the issue and spoke on condition of anonymity.

Thousands of migrants from across Africa and beyond travel to Morocco each year, fleeing conflict, poverty and instability and seeking a route into Europe. Many attempt to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish exclave on Morocco’s northern coast, hoping eventually to make their way to mainland Spain and better economic opportunities.

Tommy John, the major league pitcher who achieved 288 victories over a 26-year career and became the first player to successfully return after revolutionary elbow surgery later named in his honor, has died at age 83.

He passed away Saturday night at his home in Bradenton, Florida, according to his agent Mike Maguire on Sunday. He was under hospice care.

On Aug. 8, the New York Yankees shared a social media post written by John to bid farewell to friends and supporters from his career, writing, "I will never forget you."

open image in gallery Tommy John praises his late friend, Dr. Frank Jobe during a memorial service at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, April 7, 2014 ( AP Photo/Damian Dovarganes, File )

A four-time All-Star, the left-hander compiled a 288-231 record with a 3.34 ERA between 1963 and 1989. His career included stints with Cleveland, the Chicago White Sox, the Los Angeles Dodgers, the New York Yankees, the California Angels and the Oakland Athletics.

John was 31 in 1974 when he tore the ulnar collateral ligament in his throwing arm, an injury that had historically ended pitchers' careers.

Dodgers team physician Dr. Frank Jobe replaced the damaged ligament with a tendon taken from John's right forearm. Jobe calculated the procedure had just a 100-to-1 chance of succeeding.

open image in gallery Tommy John, #25 of the New York Yankees, poses for a portrait during the 1988 season ( Getty Images )

"Dr. Jobe, if you do your job, I’ll do mine," John told the physician at the time.

Known as baseball's "Bionic Man," he went on to pitch for an additional 14 seasons following the operation.

In his Aug. 8 message, John expressed his gratitude: "Thanks to Dr. Jobe, who saved my arm & made it possible for me to continue pitching.”

The MLB paid tribute to John in a post Sunday, writing, “We are deeply saddened by the passing of Tommy John, a veteran of 26 MLB seasons who helped revolutionize recovery from pitching injuries in the 1970s. John broke in with Cleveland as a 20-year-old in 1963 and made his last appearance for the Yankees at age 46 in 1989, also pitching for the White Sox, Dodgers, Angels, and Athletics.

The statement continued, “The left-hander won 288 games, made 4 All-Star teams and anchored 3 pennant-winning teams, while twice finishing as a runner-up for the Cy Young Award. His 700 games started rank 8th on the all-time list. After John injured his elbow in 1974, he received the first ulnar collateral ligament replacement surgery from Dr. Frank Jobe. John returned to pitch in 1976, then won 20 games three times in four years from 1977-80. He would go on to pitch 14 of his 26 seasons after the procedure that is now known as Tommy John Surgery, a measure that has helped extend pitching careers in the more than half a century since it was first performed. He was 83.”

Harrison Ford is putting on the fedora and whip again as he prepares to return as Indiana Jones in a new Disney project.

Disney announced Friday at the eventful D23 convention in Anaheim, California, that the lead of the iconic action series will participate in the new themed ride at Disney World’s Animal Kingdom park.

Ford, 84, revealed to fans in a pre-taped video message at the convention that he is the “actual model” for the animatronic robot featured on Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent, which is currently under construction.

“I’m excited for you to see his next epic adventure,” the Oscar-nominated actor said. “I’m coming to Walt Disney World soon.”

This is the first time that Ford’s likeness will be used in an Indiana Jones attraction at the Disney parks. It is unclear if he will lend his voice to the ride.

open image in gallery Harrison Ford is returning as Indiana Jones for a ride at Disney World ( AP )

The new attraction will be at the site of the former Dinoland, U.S.A. ride, which was previously inspired by the 2000 movie Dinosaur. Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro (who was the Disney Parks head at the time) announced at D23 in 2024 that it would be replaced with an Indiana Jones theme.

Riders will follow Indy as he explores the ruins of an ancient Mayan temple protected by Tsukán, the titular Jade Serpent — meaning he will be forced to confront his biggest fear of snakes.

Friday’s panelists revealed that riders can expect to be sucked into the underworld with Indy before a thrilling escape. Disney worked with Maya archaeology and anthropology experts to accurately portray the culture in the ride.

A specific opening date for the ride has not yet been announced. The Independent has reached out to Disney World for more information.

open image in gallery Harrison Ford first played Indiana Jones in 1981 ( Paramount )

The ride is just one of Animal Kingdom’s expansion into the Tropical Americas in the entire area that used to be Dinoland, U.S.A.

New additions will include an indoor ride inspired by 2021 animated hit Encanto and a carousel inspired by the El Carrusel de los Animalitos, which will feature characters from the Disney and Pixar universes.

The Tropical Americas area is expected to open sometime in 2027.

Ford has played Indiana Jones for over four decades, starting with his debut in Raiders of the Lost Ark in June 1981.

While the ride celebrates the beloved character, the long-running franchise will not be returning to cinemas anytime soon after the 2023 film Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny was a box office failure for Disney and Lucasfilm.

Lucasfilm chief Kathleen Kennedy told Deadline in an interview earlier this year that reviving the series is highly unlikely.

“I don’t think Indy will ever be done, but I don’t think anybody is interested right now in exploring it,” she told the outlet.

News.title: Police looking for additional people who fired guns in Virginia university shooting that wounded 5
News.content:

Authorities were seeking additional people who fired weapons during a shooting at Virginia State University that left five people wounded, police said Sunday, as a 19-year-old suspect remained in custody and investigators sought to unravel what happened.

Investigators were trying to determine what led to Saturday's shooting and if the others who fired did so in self-defense or if they were among the aggressors, said Lt. James Lamb, commander of the Chesterfield County Police Department's Major Crimes Unit. He did not say how many others fired weapons.

“We don’t have specific locations that we are looking (at) yet as we are working on identifying them,” Lamb said in an email response to questions from The Associated Press.

The shooting, just after 1:30 a.m. Saturday, prompted a campus lockdown and came as students were getting ready for the new school year. It happened near the university’s Quad Annexes, where campus police and Chesterfield County officers found five people with gunshot wounds outside campus dormitories.

Many students had just completed the university’s “New Trojans Experience” for incoming students. Classes resume Monday.

A suspect was found in a dormitory closet and arrested more than 14 hours after the shooting — and several hours after university officials already had lifted a campus lockdown, saying that law enforcement did not believe there was an immediate threat.

The AP left email and telephone messages with Virginia State University administrators.

Camron Harris, 19, of Henrico, Virginia, was being held without bond in the Chesterfield County jail. He is due in state court Monday to face four counts of malicious wounding and four counts of using a firearm in the commission of a felony.

It could not be immediately determined if Harris has an attorney who could speak on his behalf, and efforts to reach his family by phone were unsuccessful.

Virginia State University is a historically Black university located in Ettrick, Virginia, about 24 miles (39 kilometers) south of the state capital of Richmond. The public university has about 5,700 students and was the first fully state-supported four-year college for Black Americans. Most of its students are undergraduates.

The victims ranged in age from 17 to 23 and only one of them was a student at the university, according to police. Harris was not a student, police said.

News.title: Old issues resurface for West Ham in Championship draw at Turf Moor
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The electronic advertising boards at Turf Moor urged the folk of Burnley to “visit Detroit”. Whether or not Michigan can prepare for an influx of arrivals from east Lancashire, there were other incongruous sights. West Ham have not been seen in the second tier for 15 years. They were watched by David Moyes, who saw his Hammers win European silverware three years ago, an instant reminder of an expensive and ignominious decline.

They had played in Germany and Greece, Czechia and Croatia more recently than the Championship and will hope this is merely the start of a visit. A chastening end to their trip to Burnley was reminder there is much to rectify to avert a lengthier stay. Two goals ahead and seemingly cruising, West Ham only drew. Burnley, looking to make it five promotions in as many seasons in this division, did not lose at home at all en route to a century of points two seasons ago. When new manager Nicky Hayen’s Championship career threatened to begin in demoralising fashion, he had reasons to celebrate his 46th birthday after all as Zian Flemming earned a reward for his persistence.

The striker did not score from any of his first seven attempts of the afternoon, though he was denied by first the post and then Ollie Scarles, with a goal-line clearance, from two headers. But his last two shots nestled in the West Ham net, first a well-taken penalty and then a drilled finish after the Hammers failed to clear a corner.

For Nuno Espirito Santo, there was much to ponder. He had made a series of substitutions while failing to stem the tide. He may rue one he delayed too long: El Hadji Malick Diouf, the first-choice left-back but perhaps bound for Brentford, had not been introduced when Scarles upended Marcus Edwards, who was tormenting him, to concede the spot kick. The change came soon after, but perhaps too late. This was an illustration, too, that the clean sheets Nuno’s finest sides used to keep proved elusive after he joined West Ham. They dropped too many points from winning positions last season, and two already this. A glum, mumbling Nuno pronounced himself frustrated by “many things”.

His is a squad in transition, but Burnley had greater reserves of energy and, seemingly, more strength in depth. West Ham have already brought in £150m this summer, largely by selling Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville, and that number could be swelled to over £200m. The remodelling job in east London is not finished. Jean-Clair Todibo and Aaron Wan-Bissaka are going; Edson Alvarez was absent, too, suggesting he may be. None was involved. Nor was the £22m signing Arne Engels, a record buy for the Championship, but not registered in time. The striker Pablo, still yet to open his Hammers account, was hauled off at half-time with a calf problem. Nuno wants at least one more centre-forward, whether Joel Piroe, Troy Parrott or another. “We need more, especially in the offensive part of the team,” added Nuno.

As it was, only one recent recruit started and he scored, in Manor Solomon. There were glimpses of the quality that might be West Ham’s cheat code at this level. Solomon spent last season with first Villarreal and then Fiorentina. West Ham’s first goal was made by Jarrod Bowen who, rather than visiting Detroit, may have hoped to spend the summer in places such as Kansas City, New York and Miami with England.

Missing out on a place in the World Cup squad compounded the pain of relegation but the great loyalist stayed when others could be jumping ship, took a pay cut – albeit one that could be offset by a promotion bonus – and responded by setting the right example. It is scarcely an original observation but Bowen could be the best player in the Championship this season.

open image in gallery Jarrod Bowen set up Maximilian Kilman's goal to show just why he could be the best player in the Championship this season ( Getty )

His corner was headed in by Maximilian Kilman, resisting Aaron Ramsey’s ineffectual attempts to tug him back. It was a belated first Hammers goal for the defender, two years after joining. Then Solomon supplied an assured finish after Mohamadou Kante powered to the byline. “Two-nil to the Cockney boys,” came a chorus from the Londoners.

They crowed too soon. There were some empty seats. Relegation proved depressing and a deterrent to some from returning, though Turf Moor recaptured its atmosphere. “We showed resilience,” said Hayen. His side had a verve, even they are still reliant on Flemming, who has now scored seven of their last nine goals. Keeping him is key. “It didn’t help he scored two times today,” deadpanned Hayen. “Maybe it is best he stays.”

Even with Flemming, Burnley still have not won a home league game since October. This nevertheless had the air of a triumph for their new manager. “It gives a feeling that we've won the game even if we [only] have one point,” Hayen said. It leaves both clubs needing about 90 more, and with West Ham given an demonstration of the difficulty of getting them in the Championship.

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

News.title: How to have the perfect slow-paced holiday in Zakynthos
News.content:
Zakynthos, also known as Zante, is renowned for raucous nightlife, but there’s a far more authentic side to the Venetians “Fiore di Levante” (Flower of the East). For such a small island, scenery is extremely varied: the southern coastline – home to Laganas’ notorious nightlife strip – also encompasses the pristine beaches of Zakynthos Marine Park, where loggerhead sea turtles come to nest, while some of the island’s best-known attractions, including Navagio Beach on the cliff-lined northerly coast, can only be reached by boat.

Birthplace of the man who penned Greece’s national anthem, Zakynthos was also a magnet for literary greats: Byron lay in state here and philhellene Edgar Allan Poe wrote a sonnet to the island’s “verdant slopes”.

Last but not least, food is a powerful lure here: sit in a rustic sea view tavern sipping local Verdea white wine with a plate full of traditional kouneli stifado – a garlic and tomato-soaked rabbit stew – and you’ll be hooked.

News.title: Ebola doctors ‘step back’ from WHO in drug trial ethics row
News.content:
Two leading doctors have “stepped back” from long-held positions with the World Health Organization amid a row over the ethics of an Ebola drug trial underway in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The randomised control trial, called Ebo-Pep, is testing whether an experimental antiviral is an effective post-exposure treatment.

But experts believe the study’s design puts healthcare workers on the frontline of the epidemic at risk, because it means medics exposed to Ebola might receive a placebo treatment.

“We owe them [healthcare workers] a duty of care to do the best possible thing, and a 50 per cent chance of getting a placebo tablet is not that,” said Prof Tom Fletcher, director of the Global Health Trials Unit at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine. The WHO’s health emergencies clinical unit has also deployed him to Ebola ‘Red Zones’ for more than a decade.

This week, Prof Fletcher and eight other experts based in the UK, US, Uganda, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Canada published their concerns in Nature Africa, calling for a “careful reconsideration” of the trial protocol.

They said they are not against Ebo-Pep or randomised trials, but warned there are “additional ethical obligations” when including healthcare workers in studies like this, given the case fatality rate currently stands at 40 per cent.

Prof Fletcher said: “Ebo-Pep is a really good trial, it’s the trial we’ve talked about doing for years. But we’re talking about [protecting] the ‘one-per-centers’, the people who willingly step into one of the most dangerous environments in the world.”

News.title: Wildfire watch: Inside London’s fire control centre on the hottest day of the year
News.content:
“It’s been relentless, an immense number of calls,” says Yvonne Woodhams, control room commander at the London Fire Brigade’s headquarters on the morning of what turned out to be the hottest day of the year so far.

Inside a nondescript building in South-west London, dozens of fire brigade dispatchers field calls from the public and direct the city’s 5,000 or so firefighters across 102 stations to where they are most needed.

In the middle of another heatwave and on a day when temperatures rose to just above 38 degrees, the control room was busy – the scale and frequency of wildfires in London’s parks and grasslands are now considered unprecedented.

Above the dispatchers there is a live map, with red dots representing each active fire, sprawling from Enfield in the north to Purley in the south.

Wildfires nearly always have a human origin like dropped cigarette butts, glass bottles that magnifies the sunlight, or the now-temporarily banned portable barbecues.

But it’s the tinderbox that London has become which is worrying firefighters.

Scorching hot, low-humidity weather, a bit of wind, and tinder-dry vegetation can cause the smallest spark to ignite an inferno. Conditions like this have been described as “fire weather” by the author John Vaillant.

News.title: Inside the biggest collection of venomous snakes in Latin America
News.content:
On the outskirts of São Paulo, several secure serpentariums sit in forested parkland. They contain some of the most venomous creatures on earth and provide the fuel for Latin America’s biggest antivenom manufacturing and research facility.

In one corner of the grounds, huts on stilts house five of Brazil’s most endangered snakes. One, the golden lancehead, is so rare that poachers asked $20,000 for a single specimen. It is found only on a tiny uninhabited island off the South Atlantic coast.

Nearby, inside the campus’s oldest building, a dip worn into the stone floor shows wear from the original serum-producing horses housed here over a century ago. Around it hang old scientific drawings and shelves stacked with journals bound in snakeskin.

Founded in 1901 by physician Dr Vital Brazil, the institute pioneered the development of species-specific antivenoms Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

This is Brazil’s Butantan Institute. Founded in 1901 to fight an outbreak of bubonic plague, it now produces almost all of the country's antivenoms, supplying at least 350,000 vials annually. It is part of a public health system that has made snakebite in Latin America far less deadly than almost anywhere else in the world.

Now, having spent over a century perfecting antivenom at home, Brazil is expanding its global impact – sharing not just its lifesaving sera, but its world-leading snake research.

Specimens in a jar at the institute Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

More than five million people are bitten by snakes around the world each year. Between 82,000 and 138,000 die, while roughly three times as many suffer amputations or permanent disability, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The burden falls heaviest on poor rural communities in Asia (up to two million bites annually) and Africa (around 500,000), where farmers, women and children walk through dense vegetation without protective clothing or access to nearby hospitals.

Across the Americas, the incidence of bites is far smaller. Some 57,000 are bitten by snakes each year, with Brazil accounting for over 30,000, according to the country’s health ministry.

But what stands out is the survival rate. According to the Pan American Health Organization (Paho), the region’s fatality rate is just 0.6 per cent – compared to up to 12 per cent in some rural regions of Africa.

Latin American snakes are no less dangerous. Venom from bothrops, a genus of the pit viper known locally as “jaracas”, can dissolve blood vessels, stop clotting and cause severe flesh rot or necrosis. Bites from the viper account for up to 90 per cent of reported envenomings each year in Brazil.

One of the snakes housed by the Institute Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Brazil’s constitution legally obliges the state to provide treatment regardless of cost, resulting in antivenom having come to be seen as an essential public right, rather than a commodity for profit.

For poor rural workers who cannot afford treatment, receiving free antivenom quickly is what prevents a bite from becoming fatal.

Regional biology helps too. Unlike in Asia or Africa, where dozens of disparate snake families complicate treatment, the dominance of the Bothrops in Brazil makes life easier.

It means that rural clinics only need to stock a few versatile antivenoms rather than dozens of hyper-specialised ones. The Butantan Institute makes roughly 400,000 vials annually, more than enough to meet demand.

Yet even such a well-designed system struggles with the country’s unforgiving geography.

The Butantan Institute is home to Latin America’s largest collection of venomous species Credit : Camila Svenson

Covering nearly half of Brazil, the Amazon rainforest has vast roadless expanses where travel relies on slow wooden boats. For isolated communities, reaching a stocked clinic can take 12 to 24 hours – often beyond the critical window to prevent amputation or death.

Part of the challenge lies in the treatment itself. Traditional liquid antivenom must be administered intravenously under strict medical supervision due to the risk of acute allergic reactions. Crucially, it also requires an unbroken cold chain.

When exposed to tropical heat, the therapeutic proteins quickly denature and clump together. This renders the serum useless or, in the worst cases, dangerous.

Dr Grazziotin holds a tiny snake Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

To overcome this, Brazil is increasingly deploying freeze-dried (lyophilised) antivenoms.

Though more expensive and complex to produce, these powder formulations withstand high heat and remain stable for years without cooling, needing only sterile water to reconstitute them for use.

The centuries-old process of creating antivenom is complex and relies on a method barely changed since its invention.

Reptiles at the Institute Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Pioneered in 1895 by French physician Albert Calmette in Saigon (now Ho Chi Minh), Vietnam, the process begins by manually milking live snakes for their venom.

Small, non-lethal doses are then injected into horses over several months, prompting their immune systems to produce high concentrations of specialised antibodies.

Once levels peak, blood is drawn from the horses, and the plasma is separated and purified into concentrated vials of serum.

The new breakthrough lies in a technique of lyophilisation, or freeze drying, in which the liquid serum is converted into a heat-stable powder.

The antivenom is subjected to a temperature of -40 C inside a deep vacuum chamber. It leaves a fine powder that prevents antibody proteins from degrading or clumping.

Sealed in airtight vials, the powder can sit without refrigeration for years, needing only a splash of sterile water to become an active intravenous antivenom in seconds.

Dr Isabel Batista, Museum Director Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Brazil’s antivenom infrastructure was the vision of one 19th-century physician.

The Institute’s origins trace back to 1899, when an outbreak of bubonic plague struck Santos, a major port city in the state of São Paulo, threatening Brazil’s coffee-dependent economy.

Officials turned to Dr Vital Brazil, a pioneering physician who set up a makeshift laboratory inside an old stable at Fazenda Butantan, a 400-hectare property outside the capital.

The Institute is not only sharing its life-saving sera, but its world-leading snake research Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

To test how the plague spread, he famously let himself be bitten by mosquitoes; when he didn’t fall ill, he (correctly) concluded rodents and fleas, rather than insects, were the vectors.

By 1901, the stables had officially become the Butantan Institute. The research facility was modelled on Paris’s Pasteur Institute – the “global gold-standard reference” of the era, according to Suzana Fernandes, director of the Butantan Center for Cultural Development.

“It was a model adapted here in Brazil for research, production, and the popularisation of science,” she says.

With the plague contained, Dr Brazil turned to a slower, but equally lethal threat: the pit vipers killing thousands of farmers across São Paulo’s booming coffee fields.

The snake conservation enclosure houses critically endangered species Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

While European authorities insisted a single antivenom could treat any bite, Dr Brazil proved serum must be tailored to the snake’s specific genus – a principle that remains foundational to antivenom science today.

To produce these species-specific antivenoms at scale, he devised an unconventional public barter network.

The Institute shipped wooden boxes and snake hooks to rural communities. In return, farmers captured live snakes and loaded them onto trains bound for São Paulo, where conductors guarded the locked crates in dedicated carts.

To seal the bargain, the Institute rewarded those participating with free vials of lifesaving antivenom. Between 1901 and 1977, the railway network delivered over 1.1 million live snakes to Butantan.

More than a century later, new snake lineages are still emerging from Brazil’s vast ecosystems. In 2022, for example, researchers formally described Bothrops jabrensis, a distinct species of pit viper discovered in the high-altitude forests of northeastern Paraíba.

Behind an unmarked door lies Butantan’s Herpetological Collection – one of Latin America’s most important archives of preserved reptiles.

Dr Felipe Grazziotin, curator of the Institute's herpetology collection Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Dr Felipe Grazziotin, its curator, leads the way inside, revealing floor-to-ceiling shelves lined with stoppered glass jars. Suspended inside in pale-yellow ethanol are serpents, scorpions, and spiders – their intricate scale patterns and beady eyes frozen mid-glare.

Each jar has a handwritten label – a record of where a species was found, when and by whom. But in 2010, that priceless history was almost wiped out when a devastating fire swept through the Institute, severely damaging its collections.

Between 15,000 and 20,000 specimens were salvaged from the fire Credit : Marcelo Ribeiro Duarte/Laboratório de Coleções Zoológicas do Instituto Butantan.

Out of what was then the world’s largest snake collection – totaling nearly 100,000 specimens – scientists managed to salvage only 15,000 to 20,000. Most of the glass jars shattered in the intense heat and firefighting efforts.

“We lost more than 100 years of history about snakes in Brazil,” Dr Grazziotin says, adding that the news nearly brought him to tears at the time. “Without the label, a specimen loses its scientific meaning for us. We need to know exactly where it came from”.

A fire at the institute in 2010 severely damaged its herpetological and arachnological collections Credit : Marcelo Ribeiro Duarte/Laboratório de Coleções Zoológicas do Instituto Butantan.

He walks to the end of one of the solid metal shelves and spins a large mechanical wheel. With a low hum, the wall of jars parts down the middle, opening a new aisle.

As he steps between the banks, Dr Grazziotin points out that despite the devastation of 2010, certain parts of the collection survived the blaze remarkably intact.

“It was purely down to where they were stored in the building,” he says, gesturing toward a meticulously ordered section of jars containing some 8,000 South American rattlesnakes – an entire species’ record preserved against the odds.

Losing a century of history forced Butantan to completely rethink how it preserves its science.

Since the fire, the collection has been rebuilt inside a state-of-the-art facility with fire-suppression gas systems and shatterproof plastic containers.

In a nearby room, Dr Grazziotin proudly gestures toward a new $2 million (£1.5 million) machine: a sleek Micro-CT scanner, the only one of its kind in South America, he says.

The collection has been rebuilt inside a state-of-the-art facility with fire-suppression gas systems and shatterproof containers Credit : Camila Svenson

Rather than dissecting rare or historical specimens, it creates non-invasive “digital slices” of snake skulls and internal organs, producing detailed 3D models that can then be analysed online.

The ultimate goal, Dr Grazziotin adds, is to “digitise” the entire 120-year collection into an open-access platform.

The Butantan team is also building a network across Latin America, as well as partnerships with Portuguese-speaking African nations, including Angola and Mozambique.

“We share a language and shared experiences,” Dr Grazziotin says, lifting a nearly two-metre snake from its container. “We are bringing colleagues here to work alongside us, conducting fieldwork over there, and helping them build their own national collections”.

“The idea is to reduce regional disparities,” he adds. “If we can put all the information in our collection online, we can help scientists anywhere in the world”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool's Barcola boost, £60m for Arsenal to sign star, double Spurs deal
Sports.content:
All of the latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and more

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer live blog for Sunday, August 16.

Liverpool have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola as a result of Paris Saint-Germain signing Mika Godts from Ajax. There was speculation that the Ligue 1 champions would be willing to trim their £145million valuation of the 23-year-old, but only if they secured a solid replacement on the left.

Having done so, it's now a waiting game to see whether the rumour mill has churned truth with regards to a potential cut-price deal for Barcola. The Frenchman has been a priority target for Liverpool for the majority of the summer, as Andoni Iraola looks for further firepower up the top end of the pitch to challenge in 2026/27.

Arsenal, meanwhile, may have to fork out at least £60m if they hope to sign Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen before next month's transfer deadline, according to sources speaking with Football Insider.

The Gunners are also looking for attacking threat this summer, having missed out on Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior following a long and drawn out transfer saga. They could now turn their attention to 27-year-old Osimhen, who has been linked with a move to the Premier League for the past couple of years, only for a deal to fail to come to fruition.

On the other side of North London, Tottenham Hotspur are eyeing moves for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo and Manchester City's Savinho, as a summer of massive spending continues. Reports from the Netherlands suggest that Gakpo has reached an agreement in principle with regards to personal terms, with a £70m price tag being touted for his transfer.

Savinho, meanwhile, has reportedly shared an interest in working under Roberto De Zerbi this season, with Spurs looking to wrap up an £85m move for the Brazilian.

At the Etihad Stadium, the Cityzens are on the brink of securing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in an £85m swoop of their own, as Rodri closes in on a move to Barcelona. Having already welcomed Elliot Anderson in a £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, City have now turned their attention to finding a suitable playing partner for the 23-year-old.

Bouaddi, 18, could be just that, following a formidable World Cup campaign with Morocco.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher tells Man City to call off transfer immediately after Arsenal drubbing
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher tells Man City to call off transfer immediately after Arsenal drubbing

Arsenal dominated Manchester City as they beat Enzo Maresca's side 3-0 in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium on Sunday afternoon

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher sent a transfer message to Manchester City during their Community Shield defeat to Arsenal (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher has told Manchester City they must keep Rodri after watching Arsenal run riot in the Community Shield. The Gunners set a marker for the new season with a comfortable 3-0 victory over Enzo Maresca’s side in Cardiff.

‌



But new City boss Maresca omitted Rodri and Savinho as transfer speculation continues to surround them. Even though City have stated they want Rodri to stay and sign a new deal, it has become clear that he wants to leave, with Barcelona his preferred destination.

‌



The Catalan giants stepped up their interest in the midfielder earlier this week by making a second bid worth more than £51million. But as previously reported, City are asking for at least £70m for the World Cup winner.

‌



But as Carragher watched Maresca’s side come up short against the Premier League champions, the former Liverpool defender made clear he thinks that City need to cancel any talks to let Rodri leave. Taking to X, he wrote: “Arsenal 3-0. Man City have to keep Rodri.”

However, shortly after Carragher's post, Fabrizio Romano claimed that the Spaniard is closing in on a move to Barcelona after City 'gave the green light' to their latest offer.

On Sunday, Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 24 seconds for the Gunners before Kai Havertz added a second with a close-range header. Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard then wrapped up the win with a clever finish just three minutes after the break.

‌

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Rodri has entered the final 12 months of his City deal, and speaking in his pre-Arsenal press conference, Maresca updated on the Spaniard’s future, saying 'anything can happen' as long as the transfer window is open.

‌



And speaking after his side’s defeat at the Principality Stadium, the new City boss said: "I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment.

View 2 Images Man City were well beaten as Arsenal lifted the Community Shield (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

“I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated."

‌



He added: "We have many things to work [on]. The season's just started so there are many things we need to do better but even when we win games there are things we need to do better."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'

Cristiano Ronaldo has entered the last year of his contract with Al-Nassr after playing his final World Cup with Portugal, and the 41-year-old has opened up on his future plans

View 2 Images Retirement is near for Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has dropped a bombshell and revealed that this season will 'probably' his last. Ronaldo, 41, only has one year left on his mega-money contract with Al-Nassr, having previously admitted that he's in the final knockings of his prestigious career.

‌



The Portugal captain played at his sixth and final World Cup over the summer, as his nation crashed out in the quarter-finals with a 1-0 loss against eventual champions Spain. Speaking for the first time since Portugal's heartbreak in an interview with Vogue Magazine, Ronaldo has suggested that this season will be his last.

‌



"This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy," he stated. "I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.

‌



"Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned - what we've earned. Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

The interview took place five days before Ronaldo married his long-term partner, Georgina Rodriguez, in an intimate ceremony at their home in Cascais, Portugal. Earlier this week, the former Manchester United megastar returned to Saudi Arabia but didn't feature in Al-Nassr's opening game of the season.

The Saudi champions began their title defence with a 3-0 victory over Al-Fateh under new manager Ange Postecoglou. Their former boss, Jorge Jesus, left at the end of last season and is now Portugal's head coach.

Speaking at his unveiling press conference, Jesus said that the door was open for Ronaldo to receive a call-up, with their next match scheduled for late September. "I haven't spoken to Cris yet. He will never be a problem for the national team or for me," Jesus explained.

‌



Should Cristiano Ronaldo retire next year? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo couldn't achieve his World Cup dream (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

"As for the controversy, everyone is entitled to their own opinion. When the time comes to make a decision, I will speak with Cris and with everyone else individually. Cris is a symbol of Portugal. He will go down in history.

Article continues below

"It has been a great pleasure working with him. He is incredibly easy to work with. I need to speak with him to find out what he wants to do. He has always told me that he wants to finish his career at Al-Nassr. If he is in a position to be called up, I will do so."

Sports.title: Arsenal thump Man City to lay down early title marker and win Community Shield - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal gained an early psychological edge over old foes Manchester City by battering them in a one-sided affair to claim victory and the Community Shield.

In the first meeting between the two sides most heavily fancied to contest another gruelling title race, it was the Premier League champions who struck first - and within 30 seconds. Riccardo Calafiori finished with aplomb after rampaging forward from left-back after sterling work from Myles Lewis-Skelly, catching City cold.

Kai Havertz then made it two in the 28th minute, nodding the ball underneath the hapless Gianluigi Donnarumma after a smart blindside run and header back across goal from Christos Tzolis. Arsenal did need David Raya to be at his best to keep City at bay, while only a phenomenal block from Ben White prevented Jeremy Doku from halving the deficit despite the Gunners' dominance.

Three minutes after the restart, Mikel Arteta's put the game beyond City with Martin Odegaard showing excellent composure to sit down Donnarumma after being picked out by Tzolis.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Arsenal's fast start...and Lewis-Skelly's role in it

As far as dream starts go, it doesn't get much better than scoring inside 30 seconds. Manchester City were absolutely caught cold and left with a mountain to climb before some in sky blue had even settled into their seats.

Lewis-Skelly's role in the goal was significant; not only did he thread the perfect ball through to Calafiori in the City penalty area, he was also in the right place at the right time in his own box later in the half to prevent Nico O'Reilly from putting City right back into the game. This was another accomplished showing from the young Hale End graduate in his natural position. For sale? You can see why talk Lewis-Skelly could be sacrificed for superior financial flexibility has gone down about as well as a half and half Tottenham scarf with the Gunners fanbase. Surely there's a role for him in this team. If there was any doubt, maybe this display will give Arteta and the Arsenal hierarchy food for thought.

2. Tzolis keeps streak going

View 5 Images Christos Tzolis impressed against Manchester City and bagged two assists (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

‌



He may not have been signed to be the left-sided attacker to level up Arsenal's output from the flanks, but Tzolis has seriously looked the part in pre-season. The Greek international has registered a goal or an assist in every game he's played for his new club, a streak he extended here by teeing up Havertz following a smart run and pinpoint header back across goal. Not content with that, the former Club Brugge man picked out Odegaard in a crowded penalty area minutes after the restart to kill the game off.

With Gabriel Martinelli left out of the squad for the game, it seems a safe bet the shirt is Tzolis' to lose both for and following Friday's Premier League opener at Coventry. Yes, his cause has been aided by Arsenal's failure to land the marquee attackers they have been courting in the market. But Tzolis has looked every inch the superstar Arsenal have craved to enhance their left-hand side. All the while Arsenal are still scouring the market, he has a golden chance to lock down a starting berth.

3. City's Donnarumma dilemma

View 5 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma had a day to forget in the Manchester City goal (Image: Glyn Kirk/AFP)

More than a few eyebrows were raised when Manchester City signed Donnarumma just weeks after bringing James Trafford back to the club. Even more were raised when City doubled down on Donnarumma's status as undisputed No 1 after a mixed debut campaign by agreeing to sell the hugely promising Trafford to Leeds.

‌



Donnarumma was signed as one of the best keepers in the world. But while the man at the opposite end of the pitch continues to enhance his own claims for that honour, City's No 1 was absolutely all at sea. He was on the floor far too early for Arsenal's first goal, the second should never have squirmed underneath him and Odegaard sat him down the clincher third far too easily. Yes, even the elite are allowed an off day. But you do wonder whether Manchester City will harbour regrets over their decisions in the goalkeeping department long-term.

4. Grealish back in from the cold

View 5 Images Jack Grealish made a surprise appearance from the bench (Image: Glyn Kirk/AFP)

With Manchester City toiling, Jack Grealish was offered a surprise opportunity to take charge of his destiny when he was introduced as a half-time substitute.

The £100million man was frozen out and shown the door by Pep Guardiola but Enzo Maresca has refused to completely shut that same door when it comes to Grealish. His cameo here alone will not drastically alter his future. But if Maresca is open to giving him opportunities, perhaps Grealish and City's story could extend to a second act.

‌



5. Arsenal get early edge over rivals

View 5 Images Arsenal were comfortable winners in their first meeting of the season with Man City (Image: Charlotte Wilson/Offside)

In the grand scheme of things, neither Arsenal or Manchester City were ever going to put too much on today's game with the prize of the Community Shield smallfry in the grand scheme of things.

But a victory this comprehensive could give Arsenal a major psychological edge in the title race if, as expected, these two slug it out again for the domestic crown. Whether or not that proves to be the case remains to be seen. But this was not the polished first significant outing Maresca would have been coping for as Manchester City manager. Far from it. Arsenal on the other hand, were magnificent led by an inspired performance from their captain, Odegaard.

City will improve because of the talent they have, and because Maresca is a fine coach. But for now, it's Arsenal 1-0 Man City.

‌

Sports.title: Harry Maguire backs Marcus Rashford for Man Utd stay - 'He is going to help us'
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire backs Marcus Rashford for Man Utd stay - 'He is going to help us'

Marcus Rashford made his first appearance for Manchester United since December 2024 in their pre-season friendly with AC Milan and Harry Maguire wants the attacker to stick around long-term

View 2 Images Harry Maguire wants Marcus Rashford to stay at Manchester United (Image: Andrzej Iwanczuk/NurPhoto)

Harry Maguire says that the Manchester United dressing room want Marcus Rashford to stay at the club following his return to the first team.

‌



Rashford had not made a competitive appearance for United since the fixture against Viktoria Plzen back in December 2024 prior to this weekend and was expected to join Barcelona permanently this summer after signing for them on loan last year. However, the Spanish giants declined to trigger an option to sign the England star permanently.

‌



With no other agreement in place for a transfer, Rashford has been left in limbo this summer with some suggesting he could now be reintegrated at Old Trafford by Michael Carrick.

‌



The attacker featured for 30 minutes as a substitute in Saturday's pre-season friendly defeat against AC Milan while wearing the No 9 shirt, further fuelling speculation that there could yet be another chapter in his Manchester United story.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And Maguire made it clear that he and his team-mates hope the United academy graduate will still be a red when the transfer window closes. “He can improve us for sure,” the 33-year-old told The Athletic. “I think you have seen when he came on (against Milan), he threatens the back line really well. He could have even scored for us today.

‌



“He’s a huge threat to have in your team, if he’s going to stay with us. Obviously the transfer window is still open, but we hope as players that he stays and he’s a big asset to have.

“I’ve played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that from playing against him, and playing with him in training, he is going to help us.”

Rashford enjoyed a fine season in Spain, accumulating 14 goals and 14 assists across 49 appearances in all competitions for Barca.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford is back in the picture at Old Trafford but could still move in the transfer window

Carrick knows all about Rashford's quality having worked with the attacker both as a player and a coach during his previous spells at United.

He hinted earlier this week that he was working on the basis Rashford was staying put, saying: “He's our player and he's come back great. He's just like any other player.

Article continues below

“I've known Marcus a long time and he gives us something a little bit different. And he's been in great spirits since he's been back. He's been back two or three days training and it's just pretty normal, to be honest. And we're looking forward to the start of the season.”

Sports.title: McIlroy 'so far away' from best form after dismal St. Jude showing
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy bemoaned his poor form as he finished 66th at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, saying "I am so far away from where I need to be".

The six-time major winner, who succesfully defended his Masters title earlier this year, has played a limited schedule since, with a couple of tied-seventh finishes at the PGA Championship and Scottish Open his best showings and only top-10s in seven tournaments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Rory McIlroy's final round from The Masters as a one-under par 71 won the Northern Irishman a second-straight Green Jacket at Augusta National

McIlroy, who went into the first of three FedExCup Playoffs 12th in the standings, is bidding to win a record-extending fourth seasong-ending title, but posted rounds of 74, 70, 72 and 72 to finish eight over.

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work? Only the top 70 in the season-long FedExCup standings have reached the FedEx St. Jude Championship. The top 50 then progress to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 make it to the Tour Championship (August 27-30). Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship. In the closing event, all players begin at even par, with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025. The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

"Obviously, I didn't come in here with a ton of reps," McIlroy said. "I felt like the more the week went on, the more I felt lost with my golf swing.

"Figured it out a little bit the last few holes today but my swing wasn't in sync and I didn't do a ton of practice coming in here."

Image: Rory McIlroy finished 66th on eight over at the FedEx St. Jude Championship

The top 50 in the standings after the FedEx St. Jude Championship progress to the BMW Championship, with the top 30 then qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

But McIlroy feels like he is a long way from being competitive, with his game needing a lot of work before next week's BMW Championship.

He added: "I'm going to have to work pretty hard, put my head down and grind between now and next Thursday to have any sort of golf game to compete next week.

"I'll go to Bellerive Country Club and try to prepare for that golf course. But it's more about the execution about what I'm doing right now and that wasn't there this week.

"I am so far away from where I need to be to even feel like I have a chance so I've just got to keep working and hope it turns around a little bit."

Sports.title: West Ham blow two-goal lead at Burnley to draw on Championship return
Sports.content:
Zian Flemming struck twice late on as Burnley came back to deny West Ham in a 2-2 Championship draw between the freshly relegated sides at Turf Moor.

West Ham, strong favourites to make an immediate return to the Premier League, looked set for three points when Manor Solomon rifled home in the 72nd minute, doubling the lead given to them by Max Kilman 10 minutes in.

But Burnley kept scrapping, and Flemming struck an 83rd-minute penalty before finding the net in stoppage time to give his boss Nicky Hayen a first league point on his 46th birthday, and prevent what would have been their first home Championship defeat since April 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Zian Flemming struck a stoppage-time equaliser

West Ham may have lost Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for big transfer fees since the drop, but have crucially kept Jarrod Bowen and this week broke the Championship transfer record with a £22m deal for Arne Engels to underline their promotion credentials.

It was too soon for Engels to be involved here, but for much of the afternoon Nuno Espirito Santo's side looked to have the edge in quality against a Burnley team who too often made the wrong decision and wasted first-half opportunities.

There was less than a minute gone when Flemming flicked over from Jacob Bruun Larsen's cross, but it was a false dawn for Burnley as West Ham scored from their first real chance.

Kilman took advantage of poor defending, easily peeling away from Aaron Ramsey to head in Bowen's free-kick for his first goal in 68 West Ham appearances.

With former manager David Moyes watching on, West Ham were bossing possession as a full away end dominated the atmosphere at Turf Moor, with plenty of bright touches from Solomon - a key part of Leeds' promotion campaign two years ago.

Burnley had the momentum at the start of the second half, but Flemming had already wasted two excellent chances before he got above Konstantinos Mavropanos to send Marcus Edwards' inswinging cross onto the post, from where it bounced back into the arms of a grateful Mads Hermansen.

Flemming's frustration then grew as another effort was cleared off the line by Ollie Scarles from Bruun Larsen's corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Debutant Manor Solomon doubled West Ham's lead

West Ham's first shot of the second half did not come until the 71st minute when Bowen's strike hit his own man in Kilman, but Burnley never fully cleared it and Mohamadou Kante danced down the touchline before his cross was deflected for Solomon to lash home.

But Burnley got a lifeline when Scarles scythed down Edwards in the box and Flemming sent Hermansen the wrong way, and two minutes into the seven added on, the ball broke to him following a scramble in the box and he picked out the bottom corner.

Nuno eyes attacking signings | 'Draw tough to take'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Kilman opened the scoring for West Ham

West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo speaking to Sky Sports on whether he wants to sign a striker:

"Yeah, unfortunately today Pablo felt something in the calf. We need more options in the offensive part of the team, of course."

On the draw: "It was a tough one to take. First half, we did things quite well. We controlled, we played good, we created a lot of situations.

"Second half, Burnley reacted, had a couple of chances, but after we scored the second time it was about trying to keep the result, having more of the ball. We were not able to do as much as we should.

"We should have kept the ball more and tried to exploit a little bit more of the space that we had. But overall, the result, the chances of Burnley, ourselves, we have to be fair."

Hayen: It feels like we won the game

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Flemming pulled one back from the spot

Burnley boss Nicky Hayen speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm really pleased with the way we showed resilience and came back in a game that we actually didn't deserve to lose.

"The team showed character today, and that's the most important. They were really clinical, and we weren't.

"At the end, we level up, and it gives a feeling that you won the game, even if we have one point.

"But the way we came back was really good, and I'm really pleased for everyone.

"When you draw against one of the biggest favourites for the title, you can be happy."

'Draw magnifies West Ham's need for a new forward'

Ex-West Ham goalkeeper Rob Green speaking to Sky Sports on the Hammers' pursuit of Leeds forward Joel Piroe:

"Bring him in, and today just really magnified that they need it.

"Pablo, for all his endeavour, he's not scored a goal yet for the club. They had two shots on target today.

"He's not creating anything, so you're looking for a guy to add goals, add more creation and someone who's a target and a force to be reckoned with.

"The season's so long in the Championship, and Nuno knows this, as he alluded to himself - more options. It was plural.

"The cynic in me says this was a good day for Nuno because he turns around and bang, that's where we're short."
