Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with a trip to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Leicester learn harsh reality of life in League One but youngsters provide silver lining
Sports.content:
If Leicester thought this season was going to be the footballing equivalent of a gap year, visiting new places and learning some life lessons before returning home, then they were mistaken. Being outfought and outperformed by Notts County, a well-organised and energetic team promoted from the fourth tier, brought the harsh reality of life to the fore on Saturday.

Russell Martin’s desire to play out from the back provided the fragile foundation of a dispiriting performance for a team tipped to storm back up. Ollie Cooper charging down the ponderous Alex McCarthy before seeing the ball bounce back off the crossbar welcomed Leicester to League One within six minutes. McCarthy or the confused centre-back pairing of Caleb Okoli and Harry Souttar repeatedly gave the ball away in and around the penalty area as the team created their own problems. Things went so badly that a compilation of their slapstick defending quickly gained traction on social media.

Jayden Joseph gave Leicester an undeserved lead, but it did not ignite an improvement and they inevitably gave away an equaliser through further ineptitude at the back as no one reacted quickly enough to a dangerous situation, allowing the unmarked Conor Grant to pounce in the six-yard box.

With most of the sell-out crowd of 17,172 celebrating their own uplift, and the rapid demise of their rivals, Leicester struggled to cope with the intensity. “We’ve got loads of learning to do and we’ll be better for that, much better,” Martin said.

This was the first league meeting between the clubs since 1994 because they have been on very different paths over the past 32 years. There was plenty of passion for this rare East Midlands derby with County back at this level for the first time since 2014-15 and Leicester fans making the short trip to prove devotion is not determined by trophies and success. They also showed displeasure at the ownership that has overseen the slide and earned the right to boo as their viewing journeyed between subpar and unacceptable.

“A bit of anxiety crept in, the atmosphere changed in the stadium, and that’s the biggest learning for us,” Martin said. “If we don’t look after each other with the ball, like we didn’t towards the end, then it doesn’t suit us.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Joseph put Leicester ahead in their 1-1 draw against Notts County at Meadow Lane. Photograph: David Rogers/Getty Images

When Leicester won the Premier League a decade ago, County finished 17th in League Two and went on to spend four years in the National League. Leicester may think their reputation should mean they are playing on the other side of the River Trent at the City Ground, but that scenario is a long way off on this evidence.

The uncertainty among the Leicester defence was in tune with the club’s overall situation. A sale brochure has been created to market the club for a takeover, but Martin has not received word that Leicester are officially for sale, despite reports of the owner, King Power, wanting more than £200m. It would seem difficult to reach such a figure based on the distressed nature of the asset, despite a £100m training ground and players such as Oliver Skipp, who cost £20m. For comparison, County train at the local university and their most expensive summer signing was £200,000.

Among the misery, the silver lining is that dropping down the pyramid and selling off assets opens up opportunities for young players. Will Alves, Joseph and Sammy Braybrooke started and looked the most adept in difficult circumstances, while their more illustrious colleagues hid from battle. The trio spent last season on loan in either the third or fourth tier and that experience among those relegated from the Championship was an ideal fit. The expensive Premier League signings Okoli and Skipp were not representative of their CVs, while the forwards were blunt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I said to people it’s not going to be easy,” Martin said. “The first day of the season, we get some crazy results. This was not an easy fixture on Sky; early kick-off; a team that got promoted last year, just down the road. We take it and we move on. And we have to improve next week.”

It cannot be easy being in the Leicester ranks, with their best players being quickly sold after relegation to bring in funds and questions remaining over others. Stephy Mavididi and Wout Faes missed the match after receiving bids, while the captain, Souttar, has interest from Championship sides. Given the unsettled and youthful nature of the squad, some pragmatism would not go amiss, but that is not Martin’s style.

One of Leicester’s key selling points is, according to the brochure, their “140-year storied history”, but their efforts here will not even make a footnote. Leicester cannot assume previous success will mean either promotion or a quick sale. It is a club in a state of flux, lacking certainty on and off the pitch. If they hoped the trip to Meadow Lane would be the start of the uplift, they were sorely misguided.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta says he’s ‘fighting with the Premier League’ as he eyes rule change
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta says he’s ‘fighting with the Premier League’ as he eyes rule change

Mikel Arteta has called for the Premier League to change the rules on substitutes ahead of the new season.

The Arsenal boss was left frustrated by the size of his bench for Sunday's Community Shield victory over Manchester City.

3 Arteta has urged the Premier League to increase the size of matchday squads Credit: Getty

Arteta was permitted to name nine players in the matchday squad in addition to his starting XI at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

However, there was no room amongst the replacements for Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri.

Their omissions came amid speculation Nwaneri and Martinelli are set to leave the Gunners this summer.

Arteta calls for rule change

Arteta cooled claims the departures of the players are imminent, though, instead calling for the Premier League to allow for larger matchday squads.

Speaking to TNT Sports, he admitted: "Really sad to not have their availability.

"I have been fighting with the Premier League to extend them and to accommodate more players in the squad.

"They deserve to be in the squad. Hopefully we can change that rule."

The Spaniard previously urged the Premier League to increase matchday squads from 20 players to 23 in January.

Such a change would see the top-flight align with the Champions League, where managers are permitted to name a bigger bench.

Arteta used six of his nine substitutes on Sunday, with Kepa Arrizabalaga, Mikel Merino and Max Dowman the only players unused.

3 Arteta spoke about his ongoing campaign after Arsenal beat City 3-0 in Cardiff Credit: Getty

Arsenal transfer latest

Arteta's comments come despite speculation surrounding Martinelli, Jesus and Nwaneri's futures.

Galatasaray had shown interest in Martinelli earlier this month, with talks taking place between the clubs.

However, the winger is not sold on a move to the Turkish giants and has informed Arsenal of his stance.

As for Jesus, talkSPORT understands Napoli are considering a bid for the striker.

It follows Romelu Lukaku's departure to Fenerbahce from the Serie A outfit.

Nwaneri previously spent the second half of last season on loan at Marseille.

3 Martinelli was one of three absentees against City who are the subject of transfer speculation Credit: Getty

The 19-year-old scored twice in 11 appearances during his time in France.

His Premier League debut in 2022 saw Nwaneri become the division's youngest ever player aged 15 years and 181 days.

Sports.title: Scotland complete surprise managerial appointment as Steven Naismith suffers snub
Sports.content:
Ex-Belgium international Sebastien Pocognoli has been confirmed as Scotland's new manager.

The Tartan Army had been searching for a new boss after Steve Clarke stepped down earlier this summer.

2 Pocognoli is only five years into his senior coaching career Credit: Getty

Pocognoli was a free agent having been sacked by Monaco in June following an underwhelming eight months in charge.

His best managerial achievement to date is guiding Union Saint-Gilloise to a first Belgian Pro League title in 90 years in 2024.

The 39-year-old is now poised to lead Scotland into a new era, becoming the nation's first new manager since May 2019.

“When I first heard of the interest, I was immediately excited about the opportunity," Pocognoli said.

"Scotland’s supporters are famous for their passion – most recently at the World Cup in the USA - and I have experienced it myself as a player for Belgium when we played in 2013.

“Along with my coaching staff, I will do everything I can to give them a team to be proud of and build on the success that has been achieved already by my predecessor.”

Pocognoli isn't the only new face within the Scottish set-up, with Reading legend Graeme Murty set to take charge of their Under-21s.

The Scots return to action against Slovenia in the Nations League in just over one month's time, following a disastrous World Cup campaign which saw them get eliminated in the group phase.

Steven Naismith snubbed by SFA

Assistant manager Steven Naismith had been tipped to step in for the upcoming international break but Pocognoli now takes the reins immediately.

Naismith has been an assistant manager within the Scotland set-up since August 2025.

2 Naismith has been overlooked despite being in the Scotland set-up Credit: Getty

The former Everton star's only previous coaching experience was a 65-game spell in charge of Scottish side Hearts.

As for Pocognoli, the Scotland role is just his third senior managerial gig.

Prior to his appointment at Union SG, Pocognoli was Belgium's Under-18 coach for almost a year.

He also had spells working with youth teams at Genk and Union SG.

Sebastien Pocognoli's career at a glance

Pocognoli moved into management after a playing career that spanned nearly two decades.

He began at Genk before moves to AZ Alkmaar, Standard Liege and Hannover 96 followed.

Pocognoli then became a Premier League player when he joined West Brom in July 2014.

However, the left-back's time at the Hawthorns didn't quite go to plan as he made just 21 appearances for the club.

He eventually returned to Belgium in 2017, linking up with Standard Liege for a second time.

Pocognoli also won 13 caps for Belgium but never represented his nation at a World Cup or at the Euros.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea striker Michy Batshuayi set for 11th club of career as he nears Germany exit
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea striker Michy Batshuayi set for 11th club of career as he nears Germany exit

Former Chelsea striker Michy Batshuayi is poised to move to the Saudi Pro League, talkSPORT understands.

Batshuayi spent the last season-and-a-half with Eintracht Frankfurt but is expected to join an as yet unnamed Saudi club.



2 Batshuayi was part of Chelsea's most recent Premier League title success in 2017 Credit: Getty

They would be the 11th club of the 32-year-old Belgium international's career to date.

Having started out with Belgian side Standard Liege, Batshuayi moved to Marseille in 2014 before making the switch to Chelsea two years later.

He scored 25 goals in 77 appearances for the Blues, netting five times en route to the 2016/17 Premier League title under Antonio Conte – despite only playing 236 minutes all season.



Indeed, he notched the decisive goal against West Brom which wrapped up the title – though he was less than complimentary about his manager.

Batshuayi said of Conte in 2022: "Conte was constantly contradicting himself. To start with my arrival. He called me and explained his project. He wanted me to play in a two-man frontline alongside Diego Costa.



"Did I believe that? Of course, because Conte has played with two attackers all his career. Except at Chelsea with me. I do not understand. The truth is that I have been fooled far too often."

Batshuayi's journeyman career

Batshuayi spent much of his six years as a Chelsea player out on loan, turning out for Borussia Dortmund, Valencia, Crystal Palace and Besiktas.



He left Stamford Bridge permanently in 2022, signing for Fenerbahce after a proposed switch to Nottingham Forest collapsed on deadline day – before making history when he joined Galatasaray in 2024.

By doing so, Batshuayi became the first non-Turkish player ever to represent all of Istanbul's Big Three rivals.

His time in Turkey wasn't entirely smooth sailing, however – while playing for Fenerbahce against Trabzonspor, he was seen trying to kick a pitch-invading fan in the head amid tumultuous scenes in the stadium.

2 Batshuayi made the controversial move from Fenerbahce to arch-rivals Galatasaray in 2024 Credit: Getty



His family were also subjected to death threats before he signed for Galatasaray.

A Turkish Cup winner with Fenerbahce, Batshuayi was snapped up by Frankfurt in February last year.

But he ultimately featured sparingly for the Bundesliga outfit, making only 10 appearances in all competitions last term.

Batshuayi has earned 52 caps Belgium, playing at two World Cups – helping the Red Devils finish third in 2018 – and two European Championships.



With 27 goals, he is his country's eighth-highest scorer of all time.

He hasn't been capped for over two years, though, last appearing in a March 2024 friendly against England at Wembley.

Sports.title: Man City joined in race to sign £70million-rated Chelsea star Pedro Neto
Sports.content:
Manchester City face competition from Al Hilal to sign Pedro Neto from Chelsea, talkSPORT understands.

The Portugal winger has emerged as a target for the 21-time champions of Saudi Arabia.

2 Neto helped Chelsea to the final of last season's FA Cup Credit: Getty

talkSPORT reported earlier this month that Chelsea value Neto at £70million – £16million more than they paid to sign him from Wolves two years ago.

Man City are keen to bring the 26-year-old to the Etihad Stadium as a replacement for Savinho, who has been strongly linked with a move to Tottenham, for whom Neto himself is also a rumoured target.

Were Neto to make the switch to the North West, he would be reunited with Enzo Maresca – his boss when he joined Chelsea.

Should he sign for Al Hilal, he will link up with international teammates Joao Cancelo and Ruben Neves – the latter of whom he played alongside at Wolves.

Neto's Chelsea future

Despite starting 54 games across all competitions in the last two seasons, the big-money arrival of Morgan Rogers could see Neto struggle for minutes under new Blues boss Xabi Alonso.

Rogers is one of a host of attacking arrivals at Stamford Bridge this summer, along with Emmanuel Emegha, Geovany Quenda, Danny Welbeck and Dastan Satapayev – though the latter was immediately loaned out to Burnley.

Discussing the possibility of Neto heading to Man City, talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook explained: "Pedro Neto is a player that Maresca knows well from his time at Chelsea, and I'm told Manchester City's interest in Neto is genuine.

"This could develop if Savinho completes what would be a protracted move to Tottenham, bearing in mind they tried to sign him last summer and in the January transfer window.

"That interest remains. Roberto De Zerbi is driving it at the moment. Savinho is keen to make the move. So it could be one in, one out at the Etihad.

"I think Chelsea would demand a fee in the region of £70million for Neto – City were asking for £60million for Savinho.

2 Savinho could be key to any deal for Neto

"So, these two pieces of the transfer jigsaw could end up fitting together quite nicely."

Neto was involved in Chelsea's final two pre-season friendlies against AC Milan and Real Sociedad after helping Portugal to the last 16 of this summer's World Cup.

Chelsea begin the 2026/27 Premier League campaign away to West London rivals Fulham a week on Monday August 24, live on talkSPORT.

Man City, meanwhile, kicked off the post-Pep Guardiola era in concerning fashion having been swept aside 3-0 by Premier League champions Arsenal in the Community Shield.

They get their league season underway at home to Bournemouth next Sunday.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca has huge problem and may regret transfer decision as Man City humiliated by Arsenal
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has huge problem and may regret transfer decision as Man City humiliated by Arsenal

It took Bruno Guimaraes just five minutes to win the hearts of Arsenal fans.

The £75million man helped inflict an early psychological blow on title rivals Manchester City with a commanding 3-0 win in the Community Shield.



3 Guimaraes made his Arsenal debut as they thrashed Man City in the Community Shield Credit: Getty

Handed his first start since his protracted switch from Newcastle, the Brazilian bruiser left Jeremy Doku face down on the Principality Stadium turf.

The challenge was marked by the first chant of ‘Bruno, Bruno, Bruno’ from Gunners supporters, who vastly outnumbered their Man City counterparts in the Welsh capital.

Riccardo Calafiori’s opening goal inside 30 seconds was met with a rendition of ‘1-0 to the champions.’



By the time Kai Havertz added a 28th-minute second after being teed up by another of Arsenal’s new additions, Christos Tzolis, the glum-faced City fans were being asked: "Are you Tottenham in disguise?"

And it wasn’t just in the stands where FA Cup holders City could not match the intensity of Arsenal but on the pitch too, epitomised by the tenacity of the Gunners’ new no.39.



Lining up alongside the equally impressive Myles Lewis-Skelly in front of the back four, Guimaraes already looks right at home in a red and white jersey.

As well as his ability to regain possession, Guimaraes was also able to show off his range of passing with a wonderful crossfield ball to set Noni Madueke off on a 22nd-minute attack.



The biggest compliment you can pay Guimaraes is that Arsenal did not miss their usual midfield enforcer Declan Rice, who, like England teammate Bukayo Saka, was named on the bench having been given an extended post-World Cup holiday.

Rice got a standing ovation when he replaced Guimaraes at half-time, but the new arrival should allow Mikel Arteta to manage his minutes as Arsenal look to defend their title and bid to end their quest for a first Champions League crown following last season’s near miss.

A nightmare start for Maresca

If the Gunners laid down a marker in a match that has tended to go the way of the cup winners over the past decade, it could hardly have been a worse first day at the office for new City boss Enzo Maresca.

His side were all over the place defensively, with neither Josko Gvardiol nor Ruben Dias covering themselves in glory for Calafiori’s opening minute salvo.



3 Man City boss Maresca will not have wanted to start his tenure with such a poor showing Credit: AFP

Mateo Kovacic and £116m Elliot Anderson were overran in midfield and Erling Haaland barely had a sight of the Arsenal goal.

Meanwhile, wide men Antoine Semenyo and Jeremy Doku were stifled by the Gunners' typically imperious back line.

However, arguably the biggest issue of all for Maresca was goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.



Man City's transfer regret?

Donnarumma made it too easy for Calafiori to slot past him before parrying Havertz’s relatively tame header into his own far corner.

The big Italian was then left on his backside as Martin Odegaard added a third goal early in the second half in what was rapidly becoming a humiliating afternoon for the Citizens.

Maybe selling James Trafford to Leeds could come back to haunt Maresca and his paymasters.

3 Donnarumma conceded three goals in his first competitive appearance of the season Credit: AFP



While the Community Shield can often prove a red herring for the season ahead, City looked a million miles away from wrestling the Premier League trophy back from Arsenal’s grasp.

Maresca: We will be busy in transfer window

But claims by Maresca firmly suggest there will be a stronger City in place once the summer transfer window closes on September 1.

Confirming that he expects more signings this summer, Maresca said after the match: "We knew already before the game the things we need to do.

"We know what we have to do. We will be busy."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell statement on retirement plans
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo appears set to retire from professional football at the end of the season.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has revealed he expects the new campaign to be his last.



3 Ronaldo has revealed this season is set to be his last in football Credit: Getty

Ronaldo's contract with Al Nassr expires next summer, which will take his stay at the club to four-and-a-half years.

He will be 42 by the time his deal ends with his birthday in February.

Prior to his latest comments, the 41-year-old had said in November that he expected to keep playing for 'one or two years'.



However, he added that the 2026 World Cup would be his last.

Ronaldo statement

The veteran forward has now lifted the lid on his retirement plans for the end of the campaign.

Speaking to Vogue, he explained: "This will probably be my last year in football and I want to leave a spectacular legacy.



"I already have my entire future planned. I have so many things to keep me busy that it's difficult to name just one.

"Since football can leave a great void, it's necessary to fill the time in various ways, not just one.



"And also to have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really enjoy, and continue to enjoy what I've achieved, what we've achieved. After all, it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

Ronaldo's remarks come after he was not involved in Al Nassr's season opener.

3 Ronaldo's Al Nassr contract expires at the end of the season Credit: AFP

The Portugal striker watched on from the stands as his side beat Al Fateh 3-0 on Saturday.



His last outing came in the last 16 of the World Cup against Spain on July 6.

Ronaldo's legacy

The tournament saw Ronaldo become the first player ever to score at six separate World Cup finals.

He has also appeared at six editions of the World Cup, a record shared with Lionel Messi.

Although he has never won the tournament with Portugal, he has lifted three international titles with his country.



As well as winning the Euros in 2016, he is a two-time Nations League champion.

3 Ronaldo has won 31 major club trophies including five Champions League triumphs Credit: Getty Images - Getty

At club level, Ronaldo has 31 major trophies including league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile, he is a five-time Champions League winner across spells with Manchester United and Real Madrid.



His career has also seen Ronaldo feature for Sporting Lisbon and Juventus.

Overall, he currently has 970 career goals for club and country in 1,324 matches.

Sports.title: Ange Postecoglou explains Cristiano Ronaldo absence as Al Nassr striker watches win from stands
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo was left out of the matchday squad for Al Nassr's opening match of the season.

The Saudi Pro League champions began their title defence with a 3-0 home win over Al Fateh on Saturday.

3 Ronaldo watched on from the stands as Al Nassr began their season with a win Credit: AFP

Goals from Angelo Gabriel, Joao Felix and Samu Costa fired the hosts to a comfortable victory.

The match also marked Ange Postecoglou's first game in charge following his appointment as manager in July.

Al Nassr won the title under former boss Jorge Jesus last season, with Ronaldo scoring 28 league goals.

However, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner was not involved this weekend.

Instead, Ronaldo watched on from the stands as his side made a winning start to the season.

Why did Ronaldo not play?

Postecoglou hinted he could be involved in their next outing on Tuesday, though.

Speaking during his post-match press conference, he explained: "Cristiano is here today, and he is always present with us.

"The most important thing now is recovery, especially as we have only two days after this match, and afterwards we will determine the decision on the players’ participation according to their readiness.

"As I said before the match, we have a strong team, and there are important players who did not take part today.

"But what matters to me is that all the players who did take part, whether they started the match or came on during it, delivered a wonderful performance."

3 Postecoglou hinted Ronaldo could return to action as early as Tuesday Credit: AFP

When do Al Nassr play next?

Al Nassr visit Diriyah in the King's Cup on Tuesday before resuming their league campaign against Al Riyadh on Friday.

Ronaldo is into the final year of his current deal with the club after signing an extension last summer.

Since joining Al Nassr in 2023, he has scored 123 goals in 142 appearances across all competitions.

However, the veteran forward will be 42 by the time his contract expires at the end of June 2027.

His absence on Saturday means Portugal's round of 16 exit at the World Cup remains his most recent action.

Ronaldo's side were beaten by eventual winners Spain on July 6.

3 Felix was on the scoresheet as Al Nassr beat Al Fateh 3-0 Credit: Getty

The tournament marked his sixth World Cup finals, more than any other player has appeared at.

Despite Portugal's early exit, Ronaldo scored three goals in five matches to take his overall tally for his country to 146 in 233 caps.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire in desperate plea to Manchester United board to not sell teammate
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire in desperate plea to Manchester United board to not sell teammate

Harry Maguire hopes Marcus Rashford will stay at and strengthen Manchester United after returning to the club.

Rashford has been reintegrated into the Man United squad after loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, but his future is still uncertain.



2 Rashford made his first Man United appearance in 20 months on Saturday Credit: Getty

Despite bringing him off the bench in Saturday's 4-2 pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan in Poland, head coach Michael Carrick has not said for sure whether the 28-year-old will remain at Old Trafford.

But Maguire certainly doesn't want to see his club and international teammate leave.

"Obviously, the transfer window is still open," the defender acknowledged.



"As players, we hope he stays because if he does, he is a big asset to have. He can improve us for sure.

"You saw when he came on, he threatened the back line really well. He could have scored. He's a huge threat.



"I've played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that playing against him and playing with him in training is going to help us."

Latest on Rashford's Man United career

Rashford has not played a competitive game for Man United since December 2024 under Ruben Amorim.



A graduate of the club's youth system, he joined Villa on loan for the remainder of the 2024/25 season having started missing out on the matchday squad, with Amorim questioning his application.

Rashford subsequently spent the 2025/26 campaign with Barcelona but, despite scoring eight goals to help them win the LaLiga title, was not signed permanently by Spanish giants.

Having starred in England's run to the 2026 World Cup semi-finals, he has returned to the Man United fold and is set to take the No.14 shirt.

2 Rashford helped England to third place at this summer's World Cup, their best finish since 1966 Credit: Getty



And while Rashford's future might not be absolutely decided until the end of the transfer window, Carrick does appear to be intending to use him.

"He's our player and he's come back great," he said recently. "He's just like any other player.

"I've known Marcus a long time and he gives us something a little bit different. And he's been in great spirits since he's been back.

"He's been back two or three days training and it's just pretty normal, to be honest. And we're looking forward to the start of the season."



Carrick was still playing for Man United when Rashford broke into the first team in 2016.

The pair spent three seasons together at Old Trafford, winning the 2016/17 League Cup and Europa League under Jose Mourinho.

Man United begin the new Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull next Saturday, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner makes stance clear on Morgan Gibbs-White's future, the wing-backs set to thrive in boss' new system... and there's still no shirt sponsor: Nottingham Forest 2-0 Brest
Sports.content:
Ahead of Nottingham Forest's Premier League opener against Leeds next Saturday, Oliver Glasner has shown his hand simply by disguising it.

The 2-0 friendly victory over French club Brest, achieved thanks to first-half strikes from Chris Wood (from the penalty spot) and Luca Netz, featured few of Forest's key men.

Most of those players, including star attacker Morgan Gibbs-White, were involved in a training ground friendly against Coventry on Saturday, which Forest won 2-0.

So all things being equal, we can start to build an idea of Glasner's starting XI. In a 3-4-2-1 formation that would mean: Sels; Milenkovic, Murillo, Diomande; Aina, Schlager, Sangare, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Igor Jesus.

Glasner still wants another forward and may seek to add a right wing-back, too, but he is also keen to move on unwanted players. Daily Mail Sport examines how Forest are looking with a week to go.

Oliver Glasner disguised his hand for the opening day of the season with many of his stars featuring in a behind closed doors game on Saturday, rather than their match with Brest

What about Gibbs-White?

After selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City earlier in the summer, Glasner is adamant no more key players will leave. Nothing is certain until September 3, of course, but this was a very strong summary of the situation.

Gibbs-White changed his agent earlier this summer, which is often the prelude to a transfer. But the 26-year-old is the highest-paid player in Forest's history and would not come cheap.

Asked about Gibbs-White's future, the Forest boss said: 'It was clear after selling Elliot Anderson that none of our starters will leave the club. That's a commitment from the ownership and no player has asked to leave the club.

'[Gibbs-White leaving] was never a topic. We didn't have to talk about it – it was a non-verbal agreement. We looked each other in the eye, because we want to be successful. If we want to strengthen the squad it makes no sense to sell starters.'

Nevertheless, Glasner will still be relieved when the window closes. Gibbs-White wants to play Champions League football in the coming seasons and earlier this summer, Chelsea were showing an interest.

The Blues will not compete in Europe this term but if Enzo Fernandez were to move to Manchester City, it would be interesting to see whether they had another dart at Gibbs-White. Whether Forest would sell, though, is another matter entirely. Based on Glasner's words, Gibbs-White looks likelier to stay than depart.

Morgan Gibbs-White looks likely to stay than depart, with Glasner stressing none of their starters will leave the club

Wing-backs to have a huge role

Glasner is still trying to impose his ideas on this squad but from the Brest game, it was clear that the wing-backs will have a huge role in how Forest attack.

Eric da Silva Moreira and Luca Netz were constantly available for passes in the Brest half, with Netz having a particular impact. He won the penalty that Wood converted, and soon afterwards started and finished a fine move also involving Callum Hudson-Odoi and Nico Dominguez.

Operating as one of two No10s, Hudson-Odoi drifted wide to allow Netz to make an underlapping run inside him, and it is easy to imagine Neco Williams – the first choice in that left wing-back role – thriving in such a system.

On the other side, the future is less clear. Ola Aina is the starter as things stand yet Glasner continues to look for another player for that role, perhaps one who is a little more dynamic and more durable than the Nigerian, who has had an outstanding three years at Forest.

Luca Netz, who scored Forest's second in the 2-0 victory, could be among the wing backs to have a key role in Glasner's side

Expect more sales

Questioned about his options in central midfield, Glasner insisted he was happy with who he has and instead highlighted Forest's bloated squad.

He believes he has too many players and would like to move some on before the window closes. This was the perfect chance to put them in the shop window, which is perhaps why he played his second-string today rather than the first-choice players.

It would be no surprise to see Dilane Bakwa, Arnaud Kalimuendo, Eric da Silva Moreira or Morato go elsewhere, while Zach Abbott may be loaned to the EFL. 'It makes no sense to go into the season with 26 outfield players, especially when we do not have European football,' said Glasner.

The Austrian also revealed Forest are likely to be without club skipper Ryan Yates against Leeds next weekend due to 'a minor issue'.

Departures are expected with Glasner highlighting the bloated nature of Forest's squad

What is Chris Wood's future?

Wood made his mark from the spot after recovering from a thigh injury but it is unclear how regularly he will play.

Igor Jesus looks like Glasner's preferred No9 at this stage and although the Brazilian can play as one of the two No10s, he looks the favourite to line up against Leeds. Glasner is also looking for another striker, with Forest holding a long-term interest in Chelsea's Liam Delap.

So where does Wood fit in? Wood turns 35 in December and has a year left on his contract. With Taiwo Awoniyi poised to join Coventry, Forest do not want to leave themselves too light in attack but will Wood be willing to accept a bit-part role?

'We have two or three additions in the pipeline, let's say it like this,' said Glasner. 'It's always about the two clubs, the player and the agent. As soon as these four parties find an agreement we will have another player.

'I'm very pleased so far. We brought two top players in with Xaver Schlager and Ousmane Diomande. I think everybody can see which impact Schlager can have in our game.

'Diomande is just at the beginning of the pre-season, after a longer break after the World Cup, so he will need a little bit of time to be fully fit.

'Having two players from top leagues, who have both played more than 100 games, played for their country and played Champions League football… that will give us quality and experience. So far everything we wanted to do we already did.'

Chris Wood scored from the spot against Brest but it unclear as to the role he will play

Where is the sponsor?

Forest still do not have a front-of-shirt agreement to replace Bally's, the bookmaker who agreed an £8m deal with the club for the 2025-26 campaign.

Now Premier League clubs are forbidden from advertising betting companies on the front of their shirts which means Forest are currently without a main shirt sponsor, a week away from the new season.

Supporters may like the cleaner look, but those in the boardroom will want a new partner on board as soon as possible.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon praised by Barcelona fans as England winger enjoys 'electric' first appearance since £70m summer transfer in pre-season friendly
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon praised by Barcelona fans as England winger enjoys 'electric' first appearance since £70m summer transfer in pre-season friendly

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Gordon was lauded as the 'best player on the pitch' as the England winger made his first appearance for Barcelona since completing a £70m transfer.

Barcelona had moved quickly at the end of last season to sign Gordon from Newcastle, with the surprise move completed at the end of May ahead of the World Cup.

The Spanish giants have been forced to wait to see Gordon feature following England's run to the World Cup semi-finals, with his post-tournament break leading to the 25-year-old starting his pre-season late.

Gordon, however, was quick to make an impression as he featured for the first time in a friendly against Barcelona.

In the opening minutes, Gordon showed his pace as he dribbled past his marker at speed, before firing in a dangerous low cross that neither Eric Garcia nor Raphinha were able to finish.

Operating on the left of Barcelona's attack, Gordon made several darting dribbles and looked to provide crosses from the byline.

Anthony Gordon made his first appearance in a Barcelona shirt in their friendly against Basel

The £70m summer signing from Newcastle caught the eye during the first half of the match

Gordon's eye-catching start was nearly capped with a solo goal, with the winger picking the ball up midway through the Basel half and driving goalwards.

The England star forced a slip from the defending full back, before cutting onto his right foot and firing narrowly over the bar.

Barcelona based newspaper Sport declared Gordon had been the Catalans’ ‘best player in attack’ after his ‘very, very active’ appearance.

Another journalist summarised: 'Great minutes from Gordon in the friendly match between Barça and Basel.

'The Englishman is increasingly shaking off his marker and has delivered some fine crosses into the box.'

Gordon ultimately only featured in the first half for Barcelona as he works his way back to full fitness in pre-season.

AS reported that Gordon has already convinced Barcelona boss Hansi Flick to give him a starting role despite having only been in training for the past week.

Barcelona fans, however, appeared impressed with Gordon's performance and were optimistic about his role ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi was on target in Barcelona's 5-2 victory over Basel

'Gordon is such a breath of fresh air. He looks so electric and who needed zero adaption. Looking forward to him,' one said.

'Barcelona finally has a left winger that takes on defenders one on one Anthony Gordon. What a diamond,' another said.

A third wrote: 'Gordon will provide something that Barca has been lacking in recent seasons, a threat on the outside on the left. Also allows us to push the left sided midfielder higher and between the lines.'

LaLiga champions Barcelona had moved for Gordon at the start of the summer, with the club opting against signing fellow England international Marcus Rashford permanently after his loan spell last season.

Gordon had already impressed fans by speaking fluent Spanish at his unveiling, having revealed it had been a childhood dream to play for the Catalan side.

Barcelona earned a 5-2 victory in the friendly with fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi having opened the scoring in the first half.

Hamza Abdelkarim, Lamine Yamal and a brace from Jesse Bisiwu sealed Barcelona's victory.

Sports.title: Al Hilal target Chelsea's Pedro Neto, Aston Villa close in on Dion Suzuki after PSG transfer collapsed while Hull City launch move for Real Betis winger: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Bolton's McAtee targeted by four clubs

Bolton Wanderers forward John McAtee is attracting interest from a number of Championship clubs, with Charlton Athletic, Cardiff City, Lincoln City as well as Sheffield Wednesday all understood to have made enquiries regarding the 27-year-old.

McAtee produced an impressive performance on the club's return to the Championship on Saturday, registering two assists as Bolton secured a memorable 2-1 victory over Preston North End in their first game back in the second tier for seven years.

The Salford born forward, who turned 27 last month, has built a reputation as a versatile and hard-working attacking player capable of operating across the front line. He joined Bolton in 2024 and has made a significant contribution since arriving at the club.

His performance against Preston is likely to further increase interest, with a number of clubs now monitoring his situation as the transfer window enters its final few weeks.

McAtee, who turned 27 last month, has built a reputation as a versatile and hard-working attacking player capable of operating across the front line

Stoke's Seko heads home

Japanese midfielder Tatsuki Seko has left Stoke City to join J1 League side Urawa Reds for an undisclosed fee.

The 28-year-old returns to Japan after two seasons in the Championship with the Potters, having arrived from Kawasaki Frontale in the summer of 2024.

Newcastle keep Bergvall in their sights

Lucas Bergvall is one of the names that remains on Newcastle United's radar in the final days of the window.

While talks have taken place for Bayern Munich’s Joao Palhinha, other midfielders are being considered.

Newcastle discussed Bergvall as part of conversations over the sale of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Newcastle made further enquiries after Tonali’s sale but were told the fee would be over £50m for Bergvall.

Nottingham Forest are also expected to make another offer for the Swede.

Newcastle discussed Bergvall as part of conversations over the sale of Tonali to Tottenham and made further enquiries after but were told the fee would be over £50m

Villa close in on Suzuki

Juventus are hopeful of signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa despite doubts over a finger injury.

The Serie A club are prepared to make an initial offer of about £6milljon pounds, plus performance-related bonuses.

Martinez’s advisors had agreed terms with Juventus intermediaries earlier in the summer and if the Argentina goalkeeper completes his move to Turin, he can expect to earn about £200,000 a week - a significant rise on his current deal at Villa which is around the £130,000 a week mark.

Villa are confident of replacing Emiliano Martinez with Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuk

Villa are confident of replacing Martinez with Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who is likely to cost up to £30m - but would earn substantially less than Martinez.

If Martinez leaves, then Villa would have sold three of their top earners - Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Martinez himself. This gives them breathing space with UEFA spending rules but also leaves the side lacking seniority, especially with Arsenal expected to make another move for Ezri Konsa this week.

Arsenal’s latest proposal was about £40m which does not come close to Villa’s £60m valuation.

Hammers turn attention to Piroe

West Ham have enquired after Leeds United striker Joel Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for Troy Parrott at AZ Alkmaar.

The Hammers had an opening bid around £15m rejected for Parrott last week and remained in talks offering slightly more. They could yet make another offer but as it stands the deal is paused and they have enquired about Piroe with Leeds prepared to sell.

Dedic due on Tyneside tomorrow

Benfica right-back Amar Dedic is due on Tyneside tomorrow to undergo a medical ahead of his move to Newcastle.

Negotiations are at the final stages with a £29.5million deal in place for the 23-year-old.

The Bosnia international is likely to go straight into the team to play Liverpool next weekend.

Newcastle have also held talks with Bayern Munich over a move for Joao Palhinha but have other targets they are considering.

Coventry hold talks over £21m move for striker

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last night, Coventry City are in talks with Fenebahce over a £21million deal for striker Sidiki Cherif.

As well as agreeing to sign Nottingham Forest's Taiwo Awoniyi, manager Frank Lampard wants Cherif who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January.

The 19-year-old scored three goals in 14 games for Fenerbahce.

Neto a shock target for Al Hilal

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto is wanted by Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

Neto is also on the lists of Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea's asking price is understood to be prohibitive.

Pedro Neto has emerged as a target for Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal

Tigers in for Betis star Garcia

Hull City are in talks for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia.

The 20-year-old is valued around £7million by Betis. He made his debut for Spain U21s a year ago and has scored three goals in five games for his country at that level.

Hull have been looking for a winger after a proposed deal for Aston Villa's Leon Bailey stalled.

Garcia has become a key player for coach Manuel Pellegrini owing to his pace and goal contributions.

He came on as a substitute for Antony last night in their 1-0 friendly defeat at Inter Milan on Sunday. John Stones scored the only goal, coming off the bench to score on his debut.

Hull City are in talks for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia (left)

THURSDAY: Chelsea waiting for Fernandez bid

WEDNESDAY: Man United target Carlos Baleba on Newcastle's radar

Sports.title: Arsenal 3-0 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who lacked bite and physicality for Enzo Maresca? Which Arsenal star ran the show? And which 'unusually tentative' defender only managed a 4.5 out of 10?
Sports.content:
Arsenal 3-0 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who lacked bite and physicality for Enzo Maresca? Which Arsenal star ran the show? And which 'unusually tentative' defender only managed a 4.5 out of 10?

Arsenal eased to victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield to claim the first silverware of the new season.

The Premier League champions made the perfect start when Riccardo Calafiori fired home inside the opening minute, setting the tone for a dominant display from Mikel Arteta's side.

Arsenal doubled their advantage through Kai Havertz in the 28th minute, before captain Martin Odegaard wrapped up the win with a third shortly after the interval.

For Enzo Maresca, there will be plenty to ponder after his first competitive match in charge following his taking of the reins in the summer, with just a week remaining before the Premier League season gets under way.

Daily Mail Sport's Arsenal reporter ISAAN KHAN and Manchester City reporter JACK GAUGHAN were at the Principality Stadium to assess the performances and deliver their verdicts on the players.

Arsenal eased to victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield to claim the first silverware of the new season

Arsenal (4-3-3)

David Raya - 8/10

Good low save to deny Haaland after 20 minutes, dropping down quickly. Arsenal are a different team with him in goal.

Ben White - 7.5/10

Made some good overlaps, often his best work. Plagued by injuries in recent years but his resurgence is promising.

Gabriel - 7.5/10

Very much up for the fight, with Haaland a keen target after their battle in Norway’s win over Brazil at the World Cup.

Cristhian Mosquera - 7/10

Often left one-on-one with Haaland but used his pace to keep up with the Norwegian. Stepped up to the task.

Riccardo Calafiori - 7.5/10

Opened the scoring with a neat finish after 23 seconds. Takes up great positions in final third which cause teams problems.

Calafiori helped Arsenal get off to the perfect start when he scored inside the first minute

Martin Odegaard - 9/10

Ran the show in midfield. A real captain’s display. Sharp cross in build-up to Havertz’s header and then scored the third.

Bruno Guimaraes - 7/10

Charged around with intent. Kept looking to move the ball forward and didn’t shy away from challenges.

Myles Lewis-Skelly - 7/10

His sublime pass between two City players set Calafiori on his way to scoring the opener. Always offensively minded.

Lewis-Skelly produced a sublime pass between two Man City players to set Calafiori on the way to score in what was a crucial moment in the game

Noni Madueke - 5.5/10

Had a lot of the ball, especially in the first half, but did not have much end product. Execution needed to be better.

Kai Havertz - 7/10

Bundled home his header under Donnarumma for 2-0. Held the ball up well and kept looking to run the channels.

Christos Tzolis - 8/10

Two assists in a spirited showing. Arsenal are looking for another left winger but he won’t give up his place easily.

Two assists - for Odegaard and Havertz - in a spirited showing for the new Arsenal winger

Got his team selection spot on while being able to avoid starting all his big guns. Very promising.

Should do better with Arsenal’s second goal, parrying into the net rather than a strong arm on Havertz’s header. Some shaky moments on the ball.

Hugely culpable for that Havertz goal, allowing Tzolis to run off him unchecked in the build-up. Unusually tentative all game as well.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals that he will 'probably' retire at the end of this season as Al-Nassr superstar plans to 'enjoy what he's earned' after wedding to long-time girlfriend Georgina Rodriguez
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo reveals that he will 'probably' retire at the end of this season as Al-Nassr superstar plans to 'enjoy what he's earned' after wedding to long-time girlfriend Georgina Rodriguez

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo admitted that he will likely call time on his three decades in football at the end of the season in an interview about his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez.

The 41-year-old married his long-term girlfriend at their home in Portugal on August 11 - the 10-year anniversary of their first meeting - and opened up on the private ceremony speaking to Vogue.

But Ronaldo also let slip a seismic career revelation as he shared that he planned to move on from football in the near future.

'This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,' Ronaldo said.

'I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard. Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one.

'And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned - what we've earned. Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice.'

Cristiano Ronaldo shed light on his future plans in a bombshell Vogue interview on his wedding

The Portugal superstar tied the knot with long-time partner Georgina Rodriguez on August 11

Earlier this summer, Ronaldo appeared to wave farewell to World Cup football with Portugal's round-of-16 exit Stateside, but with his home country one of the hosts in 2030, a jaw-dropping final bow at the age of 45 could not have been ruled out entirely.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star has enjoyed a career of rare longevity in elite sport after making his debut for Portuguese side Sporting Lisbon 24 years ago.

Stints in Manchester and the Spanish capital followed, and in his thirties, Ronaldo turned out in Serie A with Juventus before a second spell at United and his eventual move three years ago to Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr.

In a twist of fate, Ronaldo's revelation comes just days after a similar veiled statement from his greatest rival and nearest contemporary, Lionel Messi.

The 39-year-old Argentina legend has been mourning the tragic passing of his father Jorge, 68 this month, and shared a poignant statement which seemed to hint at his unwillingness to continue playing.

'I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on,' Messi wrote in his tribute on social media. 'I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer.

'You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?'

In a show of solidarity, Ronaldo was among those who replied to the post, writing: 'A huge hug to you and yours in these tough times, Leo. Much strength.'

After sending Portugal into a state of feverish excitement over where the wedding would be held, Rodriguez explained to Vogue in the same interview that their decision to get married at home stemmed from the family seeing privacy as the ultimate luxury.

'We've chosen to do it in the living room of our house here where we have breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and where we live the reality of our lives...,' she said.

'In 30 years' time I want the children to think, something wonderful happened at this table – the wedding vows of our parents.

'When I was a little girl I dreamt of the biggest castle, the biggest carriage, the longest dress, a crown full of diamonds. And now I'm saying: no. I want something intimate, with my partner and our children, at home.'

The couple met 10 years ago in a chance encounter at the Gucci store in Madrid, during Ronaldo's time at Real

Rodriguez shared with the publication that she had little interest in a splashy wedding due to the permanent good fortune in their lives

After their marriage the couple immediately returned to Saudi Arabia for Ronaldo to take part in Al-Nassr's pre-season

However, Rodriguez did promise in the interview that they would in the future have a 'big wedding' to celebrate with their wider family and friends - but did not elaborate further on their plans.

After meeting at the Gucci store in Madrid for the first time, the couple donned the designer to marry, calling the idea a 'full circle' moment.

But while the bride wore a sheer white shirt and skirt, satin shoes teamed with sparkling diamond jewellery from Chopard, Ronaldo opted to sport a comparatively casual cotton suit, t-shirt and loafters.

'He's not going to dress us up,' Rodriguez explained. 'I didn't want us to go into a day that was so simple for us in costumes.'

After the ceremony at home, the family then drove to the Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima, an hour away, where a priest gave them a blessing in a private area of the site of pilgrimage.

Sports.title: Arsenal 3-0 Man City: The post-Pep Guardiola era of uncertainty gets the worst-possible start in Community Shield thumping, writes OLIVER HOLT - Enzo Maresca looked bewildered against lethal champions
Sports.content:
When the curtain went up on the new Premier League season at the Principality Stadium, Manchester City recoiled at what they saw. Pep Guardiola was not standing on the touchline for a start. In his stead, poor Enzo Maresca looked like a man blotted out by the shadow of his predecessor’s greatness.

Even the Arsenal supporters seemed startled by it. ‘Are you Tottenham in disguise?’ they sung before half-time. And then, to remind City that Arsenal are the new kings, Gunners fans turned their backs on the pitch and did ‘the Poznan’, City’s signature dance of delight. Maresca was serenaded with chants of ‘you’re getting sacked in the morning’.

It would be unwise to extrapolate too much from this encounter but it would still be fair to say that Arsenal are going into the new season infused with the belief and the joy of being defending champions for the first time in 22 years while City are gripped by the uncertainty that comes with losing one of the greatest coaches of all time.

If you want one example of the exuberance of this crushing win, then look no further than Arsenal’s third goal, two minutes after the interval. One of their two new signings, Christos Tzolis, stole in from the left and played a ball to Martin Odegaard, who looks a player rejuvenated by his World Cup adventure with Norway, and was the man of the match.

Odegaard took it first time, the way a rugby player might take a line-breaking pass. His first touch took him clear of the City defence and left him with only Gianluigi Donnarumma to beat. Odegaard shaped to shoot and sat Donnarumma down on his backside. He took one more touch and then rolled the ball nonchalantly into the back of the net. It was champagne stuff.

Arsenal had grown in confidence from the end of last season, when they dragged themselves over the line to win the title. This was a team that knows now that it can win big. This was a team that did not shrink from its dominance but revelled in it. In this match, at least, they more than justified their status as favourites to win the league for a second season in succession.

Arsenal raised the Community Shield aloft after outclassing long-time rivals Man City in style

In his first match against Premier League opposition since taking over in Manchester, Enzo Maresca did not persuade fans the post-Pep Guardiola era would be easy

Their chances would be helped if they did not sell Myles Lewis-Skelly before the end of the transfer window. Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a move to Chelsea but he was the dynamo at the heart of the Arsenal midfield and gelled well with Arsenal’s other new signing, Bruno Guimaraes, before Declan Rice came on in the second half.

A reminder of Arsenal’s formidable strength in depth arrived midway through the second half when, with his team 3-0 up, Bukayo Saka came off the bench to resounding cheers from the Arsenal support. Maresca looked bewildered as he looked on in the sunshine. He knew following Guardiola would not be easy. This match underlined how difficult it is going to be.

It was also a reminder of what life may look like without Rodri. The Spain midfielder was not included in the squad and is rumoured to be close to a move to Barcelona. City missed his control badly. Maresca is said to want to buy Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea to help replace him but Fernandez is no Rodri.

Elliot Anderson, City’s new £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, worked hard but looked a little lost in a midfield that was overrun by Arsenal’s. This defeat felt like a foretaste of the struggles City will face as they try to embrace life after the man who has dominated the club for a decade.

Arsenal had opened the scoring almost before Maresca had taken his seat in the City dug-out. Ben White played a pass across the face of the area and Lewis-Skelly slipped a brilliant pass inside a City defender to Riccardo Calafiori. Calafiori had time to look up and rifle his shot past Gianluigi Donnarumma. It was not quite the start Maresca had been hoping for.

Martin Odegaard was in particular sparkling form as the Premier League champions ran riot

Man City fans in the stand let their feelings be known as they prepared for their first season in 10 years without their Catalan ex-manager

City looked disjointed and full of uncertainty in the early stages. Arsenal were brimming with confidence. Odegaard nutmegged Anderson in the middle of the pitch, Noni Madueke stretched play on the right and Guimaraes looked comfortable alongside Lewis-Skelly.

It was 20 minutes until City mustered anything that resembled a chance. A shot from Phil Foden bounced just in front of David Raya but even though he could only push it back into the danger area, it was scrambled away. They remained very much second best. It was strange to see them looking so diminished.

Arsenal got the second goal their superiority deserved in the 28th minute. Odegaard curled a cross deep to the back post where Arsenal’s other debutant, Christos Tzolis, headed it across goal towards Kai Havertz. Havertz leapt and nodded the ball down and even though Donnarumma got his hands to it, he could not keep it out.

City had two chances to get back into the game in the space of 30 seconds just before half-time. First, Jeremy Doku played a ball back to Erling Haaland but his sidefooted shot was too close to Raya. Then Doku met a pass on the volley eight yards out but his effort was deflected over the bar by Ben White.

But then Odegaard got the third just after the interval and even City knew the jig was up. For Maresca, the match became an exercise in damage limitation. And when City did fashion a chance ten minutes before the end, Raya provided an example of what a fine defensive unit Arsenal are with a brilliant one-handed stop to deny Antoine Semenyo.

It was City’s last chance to salvage something from a sobering afternoon. Life without Guardiola has not started well.

Sports.title: Man City close to sealing deal for £85m-rated 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi, with Enzo Maresca's side preparing for life after Barcelona-bound Rodri
Sports.content:
Man City close to sealing deal for £85m-rated 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi, with Enzo Maresca's side preparing for life after Barcelona-bound Rodri

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City are close to concluding talks for Lille’s £85million-rated midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi as Barcelona press to sign Rodri.

Bouaddi, the 18-year-old Morocco international, started on the bench for Lille in their friendly at Everton on Saturday and coach Davide Ancelotti confirmed negotiations.

Lille have been fighting to keep the midfielder for one more season, but City and the player want to seal a move now, which is expected to come at a premium.

'Of course, there are negotiations,' admitted Ancelotti. 'There is interest from so many clubs. He is a really, really good player and I hope that he is going to stay with us!

'He is incredibly intelligent on and off the pitch, he is really mature. He is 18-years-old but he looks like he is 32 when he is on the pitch.

'He’s going to be one of the best midfielders in Europe for the next 10 years.'

Manchester City are close to sealing an £85million move for Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi

The teenager's arrival at City would help offset the loss of Spain captain Rodri who is set on a move to Barcelona.

The Spanish champions have made a third proposal worth around £60m for the 30-year-old and hope that City agree on a compromise to sell.

City maintain an interest in midfielder Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea's Friday's deadline passing without the necessary £120m bid being made.

Tottenham are also expected to make an offer for City winger Savinho.

Fernandez was booed by Chelsea fans on his first home appearance of pre-season on Saturday in an awkward, mixed reception.

The atmosphere turned bizarre when he was introduced after an hour, with sections of the crowd booing him while others proudly sang his name.

That continued when he had the ball in midfield, too, with disgruntled boos followed by encouraging chants.

Manchester City have been front-runners, but Chelsea set suitors an unofficial deadline of 5pm Friday to make a sufficient offer as they want their squad fixed before their season opener against Fulham on August 24.

Although that deadline passed without an offer, it remains to be seen if a £120m bid between now and September 1 would test their resolve.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala appears to FAINT while playing for Bayern Munich in extreme heat - as new footage shows Germany star struggling moments before he collapsed
Sports.content:
Jamal Musiala appears to FAINT while playing for Bayern Munich in extreme heat - as new footage shows Germany star struggling moments before he collapsed

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bayern Munich and Germany star Jamal Musiala appeared to pass out during his side's friendly win over RB Leipzig, sparking concern among players and fans.

The midfielder had just scored to make it 3-1 to his side in the 81st minute, but appeared dazed and confused just two minutes later before he was caught by new team-mate Ismael Saibari.

After the Morocco star lowered him to the ground, medical staff rushed onto the field as Bayern players surrounded the 23-year-old.

Amid a hush from the crowd, the medical staff eventually gave a thumbs up, with reports in Germany suggesting that Musiala had struggled with the 33 degrees Celsius heat.

Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer said after the game: 'It will become clear what it was. But of course we are keeping our fingers crossed.'

Director of sport Max Eberl, meanwhile, said: 'He is fine, and that is the most important thing.'

Jamal Musiala appeared to faint during Bayern Munich's pre-season friendly victory

New footage emerged after the incident to show Musiala looking uncomfortable just after scoring his goal, and two minutes later he had collapsed.

The incident comes following a debate around hydration breaks, which were held regularly during the World Cup.

Bayern, meanwhile, won the game 3-1, with Luis Diaz, Nathaniel Brown and Musiala on the scoresheet.

Musiala, who played at the World Cup with Germany, had only been introduced as a 69th minute substitute, but had to leave the field of play soon after.

England captain Harry Kane was not involved in the game but returned to training alongside the likes of Michael Olise this week.

Bayern kick off their competitive season next weekend in the German Super Cup, when they will take on Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to change tack in transfer market to match Chelsea and Man City
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to change tack in transfer market to match Chelsea and Man City

Manchester United's record when it comes to selling players has left a lot of be desired in recent years, but Old Trafford chiefs hope to drive up sales with their new strategy

View 3 Images Radek Vitek recently left Manchester United (Image: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images)

Manchester United are attempting to monetise their academy in a bid to match their Premier League rivals. The Red Devils are putting a greater emphasis on young talent, not only with a view to strengthen their first-team but also improve the club's finances.

‌



It's a strategy that has already seen highly rated goalkeeper Radek Vitek leave on a permanent basis, despite an impressive loan spell with Bristol City last season and United's lack of depth in the goalkeeping department. Vitek, 22, was sold to Middlesbrough in a deal rising to £14million, with United inserting a 35 per cent sell-on clause plus a buy back option.

‌



The Mail report that United acknowledge the view that their historic conveyor belt has slowed over the past few years, while the likes of Manchester City and Chelsea have made millions from their academy products. It's added that 19-year-old left-back Harry Amass could be sold for roughly £7m plus add-ons before deadline day on September 1.

‌



Meanwhile, 22-year-old midfielder Toby Collyer is understood to be available. Fans may question the idea of offloading youngsters ahead of a season in which Michael Carrick's side will play at least 48 matches, having qualified for the Champions League.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal rivals on notice after Man City win - 'We want to win everything'
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal rivals on notice after Man City win - 'We want to win everything'

Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard inspired his team to a fine 3-0 win over Manchester City to clinch the Community Shield - and then immediately set his sights on more silverware

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard insists Arsenal are coming for more silverware this season (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Martin Odegaard helped Arsenal humiliate Manchester City - before warning his rivals Mikel Arteta's men are on a mission to win everything this season.

‌



Arsenal swept City aside 3-0 to win the Community Shield in Cardiff, thanks to goals from Riccardo Califiori, Kai Havertz and Odegaard - his first in 2026. And Odegaard told the rest of the Premier League how champions Arsenal have the hunger for as many trophies as possible.

‌



Odegaard said: "We played some brilliant football. We showed our level. We showed we're ready, serious and want to do it again.

‌



"We want to attack it. When you get a taste of how nice it is, you want to do it again. We want to win everything."

Arteta has now won two trophies in the last four months and he said: "I'm extremely happy with the performance. We talked about the desire we have - and to show how much we want it.

‌



"It's down to the preparation. I'm very impressed in the manner we played and competed.

"There is more belief. How to do it (win the title), and what it means. It makes a difference. I want to live those moments again. But we know it's going to demand something special."

This was Enzo Maresca's worst possible start to his mission of replacing Pep Guardiola. It was also his joint heaviest defeat as a manager in England.

‌



View 2 Images Odegaard and Kai Havertz celebrate Arsenal's killer third goal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

He said: "The big part of the game was the first goal we conceded. Then the second one made it more difficult.

"I'm always concerned, even when we win games. We have a lot of things we need to do better.

"We will re-set, analyse the game and start thinking about the next one. We can find many things after this kind of defeat. We were not switched on."

Captain Ruben Dias insisted there was a lot of work for his side to do. He said: "It's obviously not good enough. It is a final that we all wanted to win.

"If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one. You need to push through and make things work between us.

Sports.title: World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage
Sports.content:
World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage

Spain prevailed in a fiery World Cup final where referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi over some of Argentina's second-half antics in the United States

View 2 Images Referee Slavko Vincic speaks to Lionel Messi during the World Cup final (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

World Cup referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi to calm down his out-of-control team-mate Leandro Paredes during the tournament's final. The Argentina captain was tasked with keeping Paredes on the field before the violent scenes he sparked come the full-time whistle.

‌



Paredes spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Spain star Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Barcelona ace Gavi. The 32-year-old only entered the match at half-time, but was fortunate to stay on the pitch.

‌



The former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder picked up a yellow card after just six minutes on the pitch for a nasty foul and spent the remainder of the match living on the edge as Enzo Fernandez was sent off. Paredes' antics prompted on-field official Vincic to attempt to take mitigating action through Messi, though that did not prevent the shenanigans at full time.

‌



Footage has emerged from referee cam in which Vincic can be heard warning Messi that Paredes was riding his luck on the field. "Messi, control Paredes," he could be heard saying.

"I don't want to...he has yellow. Control please. Always, always."

Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing READ MORE :

FIFA opened disciplinary proceedings against Paredes for his shameful post-match actions. The world football governing body has alleged three counts of assault against the player.

‌



Argentina's Nahuel Molina has also come under the spotlight for two counts of assault and team coach Roberto Ayala for one count. Molina appeared to strike Rodri while Ayala hit Dani Olmo.

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente was left in disbelief with what transpired. "At the time, I didn't realise it. I was celebrating, hugging team-mates," De La Fuente told Spanish television.

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has been charged by FIFA due to the incident after the World Cup final vs Spain (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.

"I want to highlight our behaviour in the face of that kind of aggression and provocation. Our players always kept their composure and behaved like true professionals."

‌



Paredes was caught up in more drama upon his return to club football. The veteran sparked more uproar for Boca Juniors when he kicked the ball at an opponent.

As a Central Cordoba player looked to get to his feet following a foul, Paredes kicked the ball towards him, though how deliberate it was remains up for debate. Paredes was only on the field for 14 minutes.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher doubles down on Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict by questioning Arsenal stance
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher doubles down on Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict by questioning Arsenal stance

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been tipped to leave Arsenal before the summer transfer window closes, with both Manchester United and Chelsea reportedly being offered the chance to sign him

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly didn't take long to impress (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has once again questioned Arsenal's stance on selling Myles Lewis-Skelly after the Gunners star provided a gorgeous assist inside the first minute against Manchester City. Lewis-Skelly, 19, set up Riccardo Calafiori to give Arsenal an early lead in Sunday's Community Shield clash in Cardiff.

‌



The midfielder expertly turned on the ball to get away from Phil Foden before sending slide-rule pass through to Calafiori, who finished with aplomb past Gianluigi Donnarumma. It was reminder to Mikel Arteta of just what Lewis-Skelly can do - even against top opposition.

‌



Reacting to the opener, Carragher posted on X: "MLS role in that arsenal goal! Are Arsenal really looking to push him out," along with two emojis.

‌



Lewis-Skelly - who's under contract until 2030 - started the game in midfield, the position in which he finished last season after largely playing at left-back since making his breakthrough. But Lewis-Skelly's future was plunged into doubt last week after both Manchester United and Chelsea were offered the chance to sign him, with Arsenal having bought Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Speaking earlier this week, Carragher described the uncertainty surrounding Lewis-Skelly's future as 'strange', surmising that Arsenal want to offload him rather the player himself wanting to leave. "That's the thing that was a little bit strange about it," the Liverpool legend said on The Overlap Fan Debate.

"It felt almost like Arsenal offered Manchester United Myles Lewis-Skelly. It wasn't Myles Lewis-Skelly saying, I want to leave, or his people putting something out. That's where the shock came from, not so much the players' side of it."

"I still can't believe it. Obviously, last season wasn't great for him for the whole season, but when a young player has already put in performances like I've seen him put in at the Bernabeu (against Real Madrid) - maybe over a year or 18 months ago, at left-back, he was running the game at the Bernabeu – and then his performance in the final in central midfield against Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



"You can't play at that level unless you're pretty special at that age. All young players have ups and downs. Last season he didn't play as much as he probably would have liked.

Should Arsenal sell Myles Lewis-Skelly? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher doesn't understand why Arsenal would sell Myles Lewis-Skelly (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



"But his ceiling is so high for the performances he's already put in as a 20-year-old kid. I couldn't believe that Arsenal would even think about letting him go. It does feel like a strange one."

Arsenal boss Arteta was asked about Lewis-Skelly on Wednesday, with the 19-year-old having scored in a pre-season friendly. "I'm not going to talk about speculation," Arteta replied.

"If there is speculation about our players, it's a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job."

Article continues below

The Gunners manager went on to say: "He's had a really good pre-season. We asked him to play in a different position because he played more as a No.6 - we obviously lacked midfielders from international duty - and I think he had a really consistent pre-season."

Sports.title: Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing
Sports.content:
Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing

Norwich City winger Matej Jurasek joined Sparta Prague on a season-long loan earlier this week, but endured a hostile reception from his new club's fans

View 2 Images Sparta Prague's players and supporters clashed over the signing of Matej Jurasek on Saturday night

Sparta Prague coach Brian Priske was forced to step in after Matej Jurasek endured a hostile reception from fans of his new club. Jurasek joined Sparta on a season-long loan from Norwich City earlier this week and made his debut against FK Teplice off the bench on Saturday.

‌



But supporters of Sparta have clearly not forgotten Jurasek’s past with rivals Slavia Prague. Their anger reportedly stems in part from footage from the winger’s time at Slavia in which he appeared in a balaclava while joining anti-Sparta chants.

‌



Even though he was only on the pitch for the final 15 minutes, his every touch was booed, and he was the subject of chants that said 'we don't want you here'. His side’s post-match lap of appreciation was cut short amid the abuse directed towards the winger.

‌



Jurasek did engage in conversation with that section of supporters, telling them: "I'm a young player and I came here to win. I apologise for the statements I made against your club."

Then, after the game, Sparta coach Priske, along with a number of his players, approached his side’s supporters to defend Jurasek. Speaking to Oneplay Sport afterwards, Priske said: "It is clear that the arrival of Matej has caused a lot of reactions in the Czech Republic.
