Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and who Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the re-introduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. World.title: Burgermeister to Open First Prague Restaurant on Wenceslas Square in 2027
World.content:
Berlin burger chain Burgermeister is preparing to enter the Czech market, with its first Prague restaurant expected to open in early 2027.

The company has chosen Wenceslas Square for its debut. The location will also serve as a base for Burgermeister’s planned expansion across the Czech Republic, with more restaurants already in the pipeline.

Burgermeister has built its reputation in Berlin over the past two decades, growing from a single restaurant in a former public toilet into an international chain with 32 locations across Germany and other European markets.



Burgermeister has not yet revealed the exact address or confirmed a specific opening date.

The Prague restaurant will follow the concept that made Burgermeister popular in Berlin. The chain focuses on freshly prepared burgers and fries, with part of its food production handled in-house. Its operations also include its own bakery.

From a former public toilet to an international burger chain

Burgermeister opened its first restaurant in the Kreuzberg district of Berlin in 2006. The location was far from a conventional restaurant site. It occupied a former public toilet beneath the railway tracks near Schlesisches Tor station.

The unusual setting quickly became part of the brand’s identity. Over the years, Burgermeister expanded beyond its original Berlin location and developed into a larger restaurant chain.

Today, the company has 32 branches and is pursuing its goal of building a pan-European network.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



Tickets will go on sale soon via Ticketportal and Ticketmaster.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: How Much Can a Prague Taxi Driver Really Earn Each Month
World.content:
For passengers, a taxi ride can make the job look straightforward. Pick someone up, drive them across Prague, wait for the next booking and repeat.

But the income of a full-time taxi driver depends on far more than the fare shown on the meter or app.

Drivers working through platforms such as Uber and Bolt can generate more than CZK 60,000 in gross monthly revenue when working around 40 to 50 hours a week. What they actually keep, however, is considerably less.



Gross income can exceed CZK 60,000

Official figures for Prague’s taxi sector put the average gross monthly pay at roughly CZK 38,000. Drivers who work full time through ride-hailing platforms can earn more, particularly when they concentrate on periods of high demand.

According to Ondřej Krátký, founder of the Czech taxi platform Liftago, drivers can typically earn about CZK 250 to CZK 350 per hour. At the lower end of the market, however, some drivers make only around CZK 80 an hour, which is difficult to turn into a sustainable income in Prague.

Official statistics may also underestimate the money generated by some drivers because not every journey is paid through an app. Cash payments remain part of the business.

Fuel and commissions take a large share

Most Prague taxi drivers operate as self-employed contractors and use their own cars. That means they are responsible for almost all of the costs associated with the job.

Fuel is one of the largest expenses. Someone driving every day can spend more than CZK 10,000 a month on petrol or diesel alone.

Ride-hailing platforms also take a percentage of each fare. Depending on the service and other conditions, commissions can account for roughly 20 to 25 percent of the fare. Drivers must also cover vehicle maintenance, repairs, commercial insurance and the mandatory social and health insurance payments required of self-employed workers.

Once these expenses are taken into account, the amount left from gross earnings can fall by a third or more.

For a full-time driver, a realistic monthly amount after operating costs can therefore be somewhere between CZK 22,000 and CZK 35,000. The exact figure depends on the car, fuel consumption, working hours, platform commissions and the number and type of trips completed.

Tips make only a small difference

Tips are unlikely to transform a taxi driver’s income in the Czech Republic.

Unlike in countries where tipping is a major part of service workers’ earnings, Czech passengers generally round up the fare or leave a relatively small amount.

Uber allows passengers to tip through its app for up to 30 days after a journey, with the full tip going to the driver. Bolt offers a similar feature.

For most drivers, however, tips remain a minor addition to their monthly income rather than a significant source of earnings.

Timing can make a bigger difference

Drivers can increase their income by choosing when and where they work.

Friday and Saturday nights are among the busiest periods in Prague, particularly in the city centre. When demand rises sharply, ride-hailing platforms can increase fares, allowing drivers to generate more revenue from the same number of working hours.

Major concerts, festivals and other large events can have a similar effect. Airport journeys can also be attractive because they tend to cover longer distances than short trips within the city.

World.title: Czechia Now Ranks Among the World’s 10 Best Countries to Live In
World.content:
Czechia has placed ninth among 192 countries in the 2026 Rumavi Global Relocation Index, which assesses destinations based on factors including safety, healthcare, taxation, living costs and opportunities for people considering a move abroad.

The country scored 69.9 points in the overall ranking, putting it just outside the top five but ahead of Malta and several larger European economies. Estonia took first place with 72.8 points, followed by Singapore, Malaysia, Portugal and Taiwan.

Czechia performed particularly well in the ranking for families, where it placed third worldwide. The index also gave the country strong scores for safety, property rights and climate risk.



Within Europe, Czechia ranked fourth overall. Estonia, Portugal and Lithuania were the only European countries placed higher in the general ranking.

The results are based on the Rumavi Global Relocation Index 2026, a privately produced ranking designed for people considering relocation as well as investors. Rumavi evaluates 192 countries using 24 indicators grouped into four areas: finance and taxes, livability and health, safety and stability, and settling and opportunity.

Czechia scores particularly well for families

The index uses different weightings for different types of people considering a move. For families, safety, education, cost of living and healthcare carry greater weight than tax considerations.

Czechia’s overall result is less impressive for other groups. It ranked 20th among countries assessed for retirees and 25th for digital nomads.

The index also evaluates destinations for entrepreneurs and people primarily interested in tax efficiency, although the rankings can vary significantly depending on the category.

What the index measures

Rumavi says its ranking is intended to measure the practical conditions faced by someone moving to another country rather than simply assessing tourism or passport access.

The 24 indicators cover issues such as affordability, income tax, foreign-income taxation, banking, healthcare, housing, air quality, climate, digital infrastructure, education, business opportunities, language, visa access, property rights and startup ecosystems.

Each indicator is converted to a score between zero and 100, with higher scores representing more favorable conditions for someone relocating. The same data is then weighted differently for six groups: general applicants, retirees, digital nomads, families, entrepreneurs and people seeking tax advantages.

For the general ranking, the most heavily weighted indicators include street safety, foreign-income taxation, cost of living and climate comfort.

Rumavi’s methodology draws on sources including the World Bank, World Health Organization, OECD, World Justice Project, UNODC and other international datasets. Some indicators, including visa access, property rights for non-citizens and aspects of taxation, are classified as Rumavi assessments rather than direct institutional data.

World.title: Passenger Attacks Four Airport Staff After Being Denied Boarding in Prague
World.content:
A passenger attacked four employees of ground-handling company Menzies Aviation at Prague’s Airport on Thursday evening after being denied boarding on a flight to Rome.

The incident took place at Terminal 2, near Gate C9, shortly after 8 p.m., according to Zdopravy.cz.

The woman arrived late for boarding on a Ryanair flight. After being refused entry to the aircraft, she reportedly became aggressive and attacked members of the ground-handling staff.



One of the employees stepped between the woman and a colleague who was being confronted by her. The passenger then bit him.

Airport police were called to the scene and used restraint equipment to detain the woman. She was subsequently escorted from the boarding area and handed over to the Czech police.

“The woman was late for the boarding gate, and after being denied boarding, she physically attacked an airport employee,” Josef Urban, a spokesperson for the Foreign Police Directorate said.

“Responding officers detained her using restraint equipment, and the case is now being investigated as disorderly conduct,” he added.

The incident was also confirmed by Prague Airport spokesperson Jiří Hánich.

The injured employees required medical treatment following the attack. Four members of the Menzies team were reportedly involved in the incident.

Menzies Aviation has operated at Václav Havel Airport Prague since 1991. The company provides ground-handling services covering passengers, baggage, aircraft and cargo for a significant share of flights at the airport.

World.title: Around 300 Czech Citizens Evacuated Due to Fire in Croatia
World.content:
Some 300 Czech tourists are among the 1,000 evacuees with a Czech police officer sent to coordinate the emergency response.

Croatian prime minister Andrej Plenković is in the town holding a coordination meeting with all emergency services this morning. Croatian president Zoran Milanović is also expected later today.

“All those injured in last night’s fire are being provided with the necessary medical care,” Plenković said in an earlier update on X.

No fatalities have been reported. The spokesman said there were also no reports of serious injuries among Czech citizens.

Some tourists left the area on their own, while others are staying at evacuation centres in Omiš and Split. A Czech consul is on site and is in contact with local authorities and security forces.

Fire spreads across up to 1,000 hectares

Around 160 firefighters, supported by specialised firefighting aircraft, are battling the blaze.

The fire has caused significant material damage, according to eyewitnesses, with dozens of cars and homes reportedly destroyed. Strong winds have helped the flames spread across an area estimated at between 900 and 1,000 hectares.

Witnesses reported hearing gas cylinders exploding inside burning homes, while the streets were filled with the sirens of fire engines, ambulances and police vehicles. Large parts of Omiš have also been left without electricity.

Mass evacuation underway

Hundreds of people have fled the affected area, with some tourists escaping by boat, catamaran and other small vessels.

The organised evacuation is being coordinated through the Ribnjak sports hall in Omiš. From there, evacuees are being transported by bus to the Gripe sports centre in Split.

According to Omiš fire chief Slavko Tucaković, foreigners make up the majority of those evacuated.

World.title: Czech Villages Face Water Shortages as Drought Deepens
World.content:
Residents say they are cutting water use wherever possible, taking shorter showers, reducing garden watering and abandoning plans to fill swimming pool.

Communities across the Czech Republic are struggling with worsening water shortages as wells dry up and small streams disappear after years of increasingly severe drought, according to local media on Thursday.



In the village of Krsy in the Plzen Region, tankers are delivering drinking water daily to a reservoir above the village. Some private wells have already run dry, while others are close to empty.

Residents said they are cutting water use wherever possible, taking shorter showers, reducing garden watering and abandoning plans to fill swimming pools.

Authorities are urging households to connect to public water networks where available.

The shortages are also putting pressure on tourist destinations. In Horni Becva, in the Beskydy Mountains, the population doubles during the summer holidays.

The municipality’s two wells have been operating close to their limits, with firefighters called in to deliver water.

Hotels with wellness facilities are among the largest users, prompting local officials to ask businesses to reduce consumption.

Officials hope conditions will improve when the tourist season ends and autumn rains arrive.

World.title: This Website Tracks How Many Trams Are Still Running Without Air Conditioning
World.content:
A new website is giving Prague residents a live picture of how many trams are operating without air conditioning, highlighting an issue that has become particularly noticeable during the city’s summer heat.

The service, Smrdime.cz, was created by developer Christoph Korb. Its name is a play on the Czech word smrdíme, meaning “we stink,” and refers to the uncomfortable conditions passengers can face inside overheated trams.

The website uses live data to calculate the share of Prague’s trams that are currently running without air conditioning. The figures change throughout the day as new vehicles enter and leave service.

When the service was checked on Thursday, August 13, Prague was experiencing temperatures of around 37 degrees Celsius. At that point, 188 of the 256 trams in operation did not have air conditioning, representing about 71 percent of the fleet being tracked.



Of the 147 air-conditioned trams available, 77 were operating at the same time.

The figures provide a snapshot rather than a fixed daily total. As trams are taken out of service and replaced, the balance between air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned vehicles changes continuously.

The project draws attention to a long-standing issue facing Prague’s public transport system: a substantial part of the city’s tram fleet still lacks air conditioning.

The website is based on data from two publicly available sources. Transport information comes from Golemio, Prague’s open-data platform, while weather information is provided by Open-Meteo. The two data sources are used to calculate the current situation displayed on the site.

Korb built the service with Anthropic’s Claude Code development tool. He has also published the project’s source code on GitHub, allowing other developers to inspect the project and contribute to its development.

World.title: ‘It happened in seconds’: Survivor reveals horror of deadly Polish bus crash on Hungary’s motorway
World.content:
A survivor of the devastating Polish coach crash on Hungary’s M3 motorway has described how the tragedy unfolded “within seconds”, as grief spreads across communities in southeastern Poland. Twelve people were killed when a bus carrying pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina left the motorway and overturned early on Sunday.

The coach was carrying 57 passengers and two drivers when it crashed at around 1 AM near Mezőkeresztes, on the Nyíregyháza-bound side of the M3 motorway. The passengers were Polish citizens returning from a pilgrimage to Medjugorje.

Survivor: ‘It happened in seconds’

According to Polsat News, Wojciech Tatara, the elected representative of the village of Siedliska in southeastern Poland, spoke to one of the survivors by phone while the injured passenger was being treated in a Hungarian hospital. According to Tatara, most of the passengers had been asleep when the crash happened.

“He said it happened within seconds.”

The survivor is expected to remain in hospital for some time but is receiving good care, Tatara said. The tragedy has hit Siedliska particularly hard. Four of the people who died were residents of the village, according to Tatara. He said he personally knew all four.

“It is a huge shock, a black day in the history of Siedliska,” he told Polish media. The village had held its traditional harvest celebration just one day earlier. On Sunday, residents instead gathered in church to pray for those who died and for the recovery of the injured.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

Children among those travelling on the coach

Children were also among the passengers, although Tatara said they did not suffer serious injuries. He spoke to the father of one of the children, who was travelling with his wife and children. The father himself suffered injuries serious enough to require continued hospital treatment, while his wife was expected to be discharged sooner.

The full list of those injured and their current conditions is still being established. According to Hungary’s National Ambulance Service, 12 people died, while one person suffered life-threatening injuries, nine were seriously injured and another 37 sustained lighter injuries.

The rescue operation was particularly difficult because several passengers became trapped underneath the approximately 24-tonne vehicle after it overturned onto its side. Firefighters initially entered through the coach’s windows and had freed 35 people by around 3 AM. Cranes and winches were subsequently used to lift the vehicle so rescuers could reach those trapped underneath. The injured were taken to hospitals in Miskolc, Debrecen, Nyíregyháza and Eger.

Read more about the accident:

12 killed in devastating bus crash on Hungary’s M3 motorway

Bus crash tragedy in Hungary: Company owner claims drivers were experienced, Polish PM to send special aircraft

Driver suspected of falling asleep

Hungarian police currently believe that the driver may have fallen asleep at the wheel. The coach reportedly left the motorway on a straight section after the Mezőkeresztes exit before overturning in a ditch. However, authorities have stressed that the exact circumstances of the crash remain under investigation.

Both drivers survived and were taken to hospital for examination. Police have said the driver suspected of being behind the wheel at the time of the crash will be taken into custody.

A Polish prosecutor’s office has also opened an investigation and is preparing to cooperate directly with Hungarian authorities. Polish prosecutors and police are expected to seek permission to participate in an examination of the crash site.

Families still trying to contact loved ones

The scale of the disaster has made it difficult for some families to establish contact with relatives. Some injured passengers were taken to hospital without their mobile phones, meaning relatives were still trying to determine whether their loved ones were among the survivors.

Poland’s embassy in Budapest has established a hotline for relatives of those killed or injured in the crash.

The Polish government has also responded to the tragedy, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk announcing that a special aircraft would be sent to Hungary carrying representatives of the foreign ministry and health services.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki expressed his condolences to the victims’ families, while Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said Polish diplomatic officials were maintaining contact with Hungarian authorities.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

Pilgrimage group was returning from Medjugorje

The group had travelled from Poland’s Podkarpackie (Subcarpathian) Voivodeship and was returning from Medjugorje, the famous Catholic pilgrimage site in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Many of those on board came from the area around Strzyżów. The mayor of Strzyżów said 11 people from the municipality had taken part in the pilgrimage.

The disaster has also left those who cancelled their trip at the last minute confronting an unbearable sense of relief and shock.

One Polish man, identified as Wiesław, had planned to join the pilgrimage but cancelled for family reasons shortly before departure. Several of his acquaintances were on the coach.

After the crash, the husband of one of the victims called him and told him that his wife had died.

The tragedy is particularly painful given that this was not the first deadly crash involving Polish pilgrims travelling to Medjugorje in Hungary. In 2002, a Polish coach travelling towards the pilgrimage site crashed near Balatonszentgyörgy, killing 19 people and injuring 32, according to Index.

World.title: Budapest’s bike-sharing chaos could leave unsuspecting riders facing hefty fines
World.content:
Budapest’s newly relaunched MOL Bubi bike-sharing system is facing a growing problem: bicycles are increasingly being left outside designated docking points, potentially exposing unsuspecting users to surcharges of tens of thousands of forints.

The confusion is partly linked to missing or temporarily unavailable docking stations, particularly in the city centre. Several popular locations have stopped operating because of outstanding permits and disputes over public-space use.

Missing stations leave riders confused

One of the most notable examples is at Déli railway station, where a previously popular Bubi station is currently unavailable. During the service’s temporary suspension, other micromobility providers occupied the site under valid public-space agreements, reports Telex.

The Budapest Transport Centre (BKK) has also yet to receive all the approvals required to redesign and reopen the station. If everything goes according to plan, the location could receive a new public-space permit from 1 October at the earliest.

A similar situation has developed around Clark Ádám Square. The Bubi app shows that there are effectively no official Bubi stations between Széll Kálmán Square and the Elizabeth Bridge. In the 5th District, 11 planned stations are also awaiting approvals, with their construction expected in September, although their opening will depend on further permissions.

Riders may mistake other points for Bubi locations

The confusion is not limited to missing stations. Some users reportedly mistake collection points belonging to other services for valid Bubi drop-off locations. Manfréd collection points, for example, can contain older-generation Bubi bicycles, while Mobi points are currently used mainly by scooter services. This can make it difficult for users to distinguish where a new-generation Bubi bicycle can legitimately be left.

The BKK acknowledged that several factors are contributing to the problem, including the incomplete integration of Mobi points and the missing stations in the 1st and 5th districts. The transport authority said users are also still becoming familiar with the new network and its rules.

Stay up-to-date: Woman abused by man in Budapest in broad daylight, authorities do nothing

205 of 222 stations currently operating

Despite the disruption, the vast majority of the original network remains operational. Of the former 222 Bubi docking stations in Budapest, 205 – around 92 per cent – are currently operating. However, the biggest expansion is expected this autumn, when Mobi points are gradually integrated into the Bubi network.

Around 1,000 additional pick-up and drop-off points are expected to become available, shared by bicycle and scooter services. The expanded network is also planned to cover major transport hubs with at least 30,000 daily journeys, including all metro stations.

This will extend Bubi well beyond its current central coverage, reaching areas including József Attila-lakótelep, Angyalföld, Őrmező, Tisztviselőtelep, Századosnegyed, Örs vezér tere, Kőbánya-Kispest, Újpest-városkapu and Zugló. For now, however, riders are being left to navigate a confusing network where parking in the wrong place can potentially result in a substantial surcharge.

World.title: Cold front brings rain to Hungary on Monday to finally ease summer heat
World.content:
Hungary’s long spell of hot, settled weather is set to end on Monday as a cold front moves into the Carpathian Basin, bringing showers, thunderstorms, strong winds and cooler temperatures.

According to HungaroMet, atmospheric activity has already increased to the north and west of Hungary. The associated precipitation zone reached the Alps on Sunday, with showers and thunderstorms developing in several areas. Cooler air masses of oceanic origin are following the system and will soon reach Hungary.

Sunday remains hot

Sunday will remain mostly sunny and hot, with afternoon temperatures of 33–36°C. Clouds will gradually increase from the north-west later in the day, with showers and thunderstorms possible near the border.

The southerly wind will strengthen in many areas before easing during the evening. Overnight temperatures are expected to remain between 15 and 22°C.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Storms arrive in Hungary on Monday

The cold front will move across Hungary on Monday, bringing increasing cloud cover and showers and thunderstorms to more areas. The Great Plain may still enjoy several hours of sunshine.

The wind will turn north-westerly and become fresh to strong, while thunderstorms could bring gale-force gusts locally. Hail and torrential downpours are also possible. Temperatures will range from 27–36°C, with the hottest conditions expected in the south-east.

According to Időkép, some storms could organise into lines. However, the rainfall will be highly uneven, meaning the change is unlikely to end Hungary’s prolonged drought. Locally, more than 15–20 millimetres could fall, but most areas may receive only a few millimetres, while parts of central Hungary could remain dry.

There is better news for the Danube: 50–80 millimetres of rain could fall in parts of Lower and Upper Austria within the river’s catchment, potentially slowing or halting its current decline.

Stay up-to-date: Nearly 70 firefighters tackle forest fire in Hungary after power line failure

Cooler Tuesday ahead

By Tuesday, cloud cover should decrease across much of Hungary, although showers may linger in the south and east. Strong northerly and north-westerly winds are expected. Morning temperatures will fall to 11–17°C, with afternoon highs of 23–28°C.

The rest of the week should remain partly sunny and unsettled, with temperatures rising again to 28–33°C on Wednesday and 29–34°C on Thursday. Further showers and thunderstorms may develop from Thursday, while another stronger front could arrive around Friday.

World.title: India’s Independence Day in Budapest highlights the deep Hungarian ties behind the celebration
World.content:
India’s 80th Independence Day was marked in Budapest on 15 August with a ceremony that celebrated not only India’s freedom, but also the longstanding cultural links between India and Hungary.

The flag was hoisted at 9 AM at the Embassy of India, followed by a performance of Vande Mataram, India’s national song, by Hungarian friends of India alongside members of the Indian community. Certificates of Appreciation were also presented beside the flagpole.

The ceremony is featured in a new video produced by Magyar Minute, including an exclusive one-on-one interview with Indian Ambassador to Hungary Anshuman Gaur.

India’s Ambassador to Budapest Anshuman Gaur

‘Life is dear, but liberty is dearer’

One of the most striking elements of the celebration was the distinctly Hungarian thread running through the event. Ahead of the flag-hoisting ceremony, the embassy quoted Hungarian poet Sándor Petőfi, whose famous words – “life is dear, but liberty is dearer” – were presented as a message that resonates with both nations.

The connection between the two countries was also reflected in the cultural centre of the Indian Embassy in Budapest, which bears the name of Amrita Sher-Gil, one of India’s most celebrated modern artists.

Sher-Gil was born in Budapest on 30 January 1913 to a Hungarian mother and Sikh father. She later became a major figure in Indian art, and in 1976 the Archaeological Survey of India designated her works as National Art Treasures, meaning paintings held in India cannot be taken out of the country.

India’s 80th Independence Day Budapest India’s 80th Independence Day Budapest

Ambassador speaks about India, Hungary and freedom

In the interview, Ambassador Anshuman Gaur reflects on what India’s Independence Day means to him personally and what he hopes Hungarians will understand about his country.

Gaur has been a member of the Indian Foreign Service since 2001 and served as India’s Chief of Protocol between 2022 and 2025. He is also a published poet: his collection Isthmus of Time was launched in New Delhi in July 2017 by then Vice President M. Hamid Ansari.

The ambassador concludes the interview with a recitation of verses by renowned Indian poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, conveying the idea that Bharat is not simply the name of a territory, but the spirit of freedom and democracy within its people.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

80 years of Indian independence

India’s 80th Independence Day marks 79 completed years since the country gained independence from British rule on 15 August 1947.

The celebrations in Budapest also highlighted the importance of Vande Mataram, which first appeared in print in the Bengali journal Bangadarshan in November 1875. The song marked its 150th anniversary on 7 November 2025, with a year-long commemorative programme running until 7 November 2026.

The Indian community in Hungary has also grown significantly over recent years. According to the embassy, around 8,700 Indian nationals live in Hungary, including more than 2,000 in Budapest. Approximately 1,200 Indian students are studying in Budapest, Pécs, Szeged, Miskolc and Debrecen.

Certificates of Appreciation being handed out at India’s 80th Independence Day celebration in Budapest

The ceremony therefore offered more than a traditional Independence Day celebration: it provided a glimpse into the cultural connections that have brought Indian and Hungarian communities closer together.

Watch the full interview and Independence Day ceremony in the video above. The video features English, Hungarian, Italian, German and Chinese selectable subtitle tracks, with the Hindi-language sections translated into each language.

World.title: Bus crash tragedy in Hungary: Company owner claims drivers were experienced, Polish PM to send special aircraft
World.content:
The owner of the Polish coach company whose bus crashed on Hungary’s M3 motorway has spoken about the two drivers involved, saying both were experienced employees who had worked for the company for several years.

The company’s owner immediately travelled to Hungary

Tadeusz Dykas, owner of Firma Transportowa Michael in Jasło, confirmed that the overturned Polish-registered bus belonged to his company. He and members of his staff have travelled to Hungary following the crash, while the wreck remains secured by the Hungarian authorities as the investigation continues.

The bus was carrying Polish pilgrims returning home from Bosnia and Herzegovina when it left the motorway and overturned at around 1 AM on Sunday between Mezőkeresztes and Mezőnagymihály, near kilometre 139 of the M3.

Twelve people were killed in the tragedy. According to the information currently available, one person suffered life-threatening injuries, nine sustained serious injuries and 37 others suffered less serious injuries.

Both drivers survived the crash

Dykas told Polish news outlet money.pl that the bus was being driven by two drivers, both of whom survived the accident. One of them, however, was seriously injured. The company owner said both drivers were experienced and had been employed by Firma Transportowa Michael for several years.

The circumstances surrounding the crash remain under investigation. Hungarian police have reportedly considered driver fatigue and the possibility that the driver fell asleep at the wheel as one potential explanation, but this has not been confirmed.

Investigators are expected to examine a number of possible causes before drawing conclusions, which include whether the driver fell asleep or became unwell, whether a technical failure occurred, how fast the bus was travelling, when the driver lost control and whether the second driver was in the driving cabin at the time.

Company sends replacement coach to Hungary

Firma Transportowa Michael immediately sent a replacement bus to Hungary to help return survivors to Poland, according to Dykas. The company owner and his colleagues are currently at the crash site, but have not been able to inspect the wreck themselves because it has been secured by Hungarian authorities as part of the investigation.

The crash has triggered a major response on both sides of the border, with Polish authorities also launching their own investigation. Waldemar Żurek, Poland’s Minister of Justice and Prosecutor General, said the Polish side would work fully with Hungarian authorities to establish exactly what happened.

Polish authorities send support to Hungary

Polish officials have been coordinating assistance for those affected by the tragedy. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk spoke with Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar following the crash. Magyar said he had expressed his condolences to the Polish people and thanked Hungarian rescuers and doctors for their assistance.

Tusk subsequently announced that Poland would send a special aircraft to Hungary carrying Foreign Ministry and healthcare personnel, ensuring that those affected by the accident could receive the necessary medical and consular support. A crisis team was also convened in Rzeszów, the capital of Poland’s Podkarpackie Voivodeship, from where many of the pilgrims originated.

According to regional authorities, the pilgrimage had been organised by a parish in Strzyżów and included residents from several districts of the region. Decisions on transporting injured survivors back to Poland will be made according to medical advice, potentially using ambulances, coaches or air transport.

Investigation continues into cause of tragedy

Poland’s Foreign Ministry confirmed that all 56 passengers and both drivers were injured in the crash, while 12 people died. Polish officials have said that several of the injured remain in very serious condition. The Polish district prosecutor’s office with jurisdiction over the case has opened its own investigation.

Authorities in Poland say they are taking immediate steps to establish the circumstances and causes of the disaster and will co-operate fully with their Hungarian counterparts.

The Polish embassy in Budapest has also established a dedicated telephone line for relatives of people who were travelling on the bus. For now, investigators are examining multiple possible explanations for the crash. While driver fatigue has been raised as one possibility, no definitive cause has yet been established.

World.title: Nearly 70 firefighters tackle forest fire in Hungary after power line failure
World.content:
Firefighters have brought under control a forest fire in the Kőszeg Mountains after a major operation that continued until late Saturday night, with difficult terrain making the blaze particularly challenging to tackle.

The fire broke out in the early evening of 15 August in the area around the Stájer-houses and the Vöröskereszt, beneath Írott-kő. Initial reports said roughly one hectare of undergrowth was burning. According to the latest information from the Vas County Disaster Management Directorate, a fallen high-voltage power line may have caused the dry undergrowth in the forest to catch fire.

Nearly 70 firefighters involved in operation

The response was mounted at an elevated alert level, involving 16 firefighting vehicles and nearly 70 professional, municipal and volunteer firefighters. Several water jets were initially used to prevent the flames from spreading. However, the terrain presented a major obstacle: the fire engines could not reach the affected area directly, meaning firefighters had to approach the site on foot.

Long stretches of hose had to be laid through the forest to bring water to the fire. Crews also worked with backpack pumps and hand tools to extinguish glowing and smouldering sections. Two water-tanker firefighting vehicles operated continuously to maintain the water supply, writes VAOL.hu.

Civilian drone and forestry teams also helped

The operation required assistance beyond the firefighting crews themselves. Firefighters used floodlights and battery-powered lighting to illuminate the area as work continued into the evening. A civilian drone helped crews survey the fire from above, while forestry specialists assisted on the ground.

Civilian water tankers also contributed to maintaining supplies for the firefighting operation. The difficult conditions and the dry vegetation had raised concerns that the flames could spread rapidly through the surrounding woodland. Earlier reports had warned people not to head into the mountains so they would not obstruct emergency crews.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Fire contained after hours of work

Firefighters managed to contain the blaze, although follow-up work continued until late in the evening to deal with remaining hot spots. Earlier reports indicated that several points of fire had been identified in the affected area. The fire was reportedly in a less dense section of woodland rather than the area’s pine forest, a factor considered more favourable in terms of preventing rapid spread.

The Kőszeg Municipal Fire Brigade reported shortly before midnight that the operation had been successfully completed and its crews had returned to their station. The latest reports indicate that no residential area was in danger. Authorities have not definitively established the cause of the fire, although a fallen power line is currently considered a possible explanation.

World.title: Woman abused by man in Budapest in broad daylight, authorities do nothing
World.content:
A woman was allegedly pinned against a wall and strangled by her former partner in broad daylight near Budapest’s Lehel Square, according to a social media account shared by actor and women’s rights activist Áron Molnár. Two women reportedly intervened to help the victim, who was allegedly being forcibly kissed and threatened.

Woman strangled in broad daylight in Budapest as witnesses intervene

The incident is said to have happened on 14 August at the Bulcsú Street exit of the Lehel Square metro station. According to the account published by Eszter Spira and subsequently shared by Molnár, the alleged attacker grabbed the woman by the neck, pressed her against a wall and attempted to kiss her against her will.

Most passers-by reportedly continued walking, but Spira and another woman stepped in after seeing what was happening.

Two bystanders reportedly helped the woman escape

According to Spira’s account, the two women approached the victim, took hold of her hands and urged her to come with them. The man allegedly shouted that the incident was a “family matter”. After the woman managed to get away from him, he reportedly threatened to kill the two women who had intervened.

The women then shouted for help. The alleged attacker reportedly backed off, allowing them and the victim to flee towards the entrance of Lehel Market, where they contacted Budapest police. Spira said the victim told her that the man was her former partner and that she had experienced months of abuse at his hands. A 60-day restraining order was reportedly already in force against him.

The victim also allegedly said that the man had continued to harass and threaten her after their relationship ended. According to the account, he attacked her outside her workplace on the day of the incident and then forcibly took her towards the metro station.

Alleged attacker was released by Budapest police

Spira said officers arrested the man at the scene and took both the victim and witnesses to Budapest’s 13th District Police Headquarters. However, she claims that after around four hours of waiting, they were told that neither the victim nor the witnesses would be questioned that day and that the man would be released.

The account also alleges that attempts were made to obtain urgent assistance from organisations supporting women who have experienced violence, including emergency accommodation, protection and legal help, but that no immediate solution was found. These claims have been made in social media posts; the information provided for this article does not include a police statement or an independent account of the investigation.

Activist calls for tougher protection for women

Molnár, who shared Spira’s account on Facebook, described the events as “unfathomable” and questioned why authorities were unable to provide stronger protection in such a case. He argued that women and children should be protected by the strictest possible laws and called for tougher action against relationship and domestic violence.

Molnár also cited figures in his post claiming that a woman dies every day as a result of relationship violence and that only a fraction of cases are reported and lead to proceedings.

“I’m angry at the helplessness,” Molnár wrote, arguing that the current political moment should be used to introduce stronger measures to protect women, especially because the incident in Budapest has shown again how victims of domestic violence are protected when a restraining order is already in place, and about what safeguards are available immediately after a reported attack.

If you or someone you know might be in danger, you can reach out for the Women For Women Together Against Violence Association (NANE) Association’s helpline for abused women and children toll-free at +36-80-505-101 (Mon., Wed., Fri.: 6:00 PM–10:00 PM, Tues.: 10:00 AM–10:00 PM, Wed.: 12:00 PM–4:00 PM). You can find further information about the association’s support services on their website. From abroad, the association’s helpline can be reached at +36-1-267-4900.

World.title: BREAKING: 12 killed in devastating bus crash on Hungary’s M3 motorway
World.content:
Twelve people have been killed and dozens injured after a Polish-registered tourist bus crashed on Hungary’s M3 motorway near Mezőkeresztes early on Sunday morning.

According to police, the accident happened at around 1 AM on 16 August on the motorway’s carriageway towards Nyíregyháza, shortly after the Mezőkeresztes exit. The coach left the road and overturned in a ditch.

Police said their current information suggests that the driver may have fallen asleep at the wheel. The driver is being taken into police custody.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

Dozens injured in the crash

The National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) said 14 ambulance units were dispatched to the scene under the mass-casualty protocol.

Twelve people died in the accident.

One person was treated with life-threatening injuries, nine suffered serious injuries, while another 37 people sustained less serious injuries.

The injured were treated at the scene before being taken to hospitals in Miskolc, Debrecen, Nyíregyháza and Eger. The disaster management authority said 57 passengers and two drivers had been travelling on the tourist coach.

The rescue operation was particularly difficult because several passengers were trapped beneath the overturned vehicle. By around 3 AM, firefighters had rescued 35 people from the bus.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

Rescue operation required cranes

The 24-tonne coach had to be moved to allow rescuers to reach people trapped underneath it. Civilian cranes were called to the scene, while firefighters used winches to lift the rear axle of the vehicle until the cranes arrived.

A heated bus was also sent to the scene to provide shelter for those affected by the crash, while a replacement coach was dispatched from Poland.

The motorway was closed in the affected area while police investigated the crash and rescue crews worked at the scene. Traffic was diverted off the M3 at Mezőkeresztes, with drivers able to rejoin the motorway at Emőd.

Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway in tragic accident. Photo: MTI

Polish authorities in contact with Hungary

The tragedy prompted condolences from Hungarian and Polish officials. Prime Minister Péter Magyar expressed his condolences to the victims’ families and thanked the emergency services and civilians involved in the rescue operation.

Hungary’s Foreign Minister Anita Orbán said Hungarian authorities were carrying out the necessary rescue and medical procedures, while the Polish embassy was continuously working on matters concerning the Polish citizens affected by the accident.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki also expressed his condolences to the families of those killed, describing the crash as an unimaginable tragedy. Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said Polish diplomatic officials were in contact with the Hungarian authorities.

The investigation and technical rescue operation are ongoing.

World.title: Romanian swimmer David Popovici claims third European 200m freestyle title after 100m triumph
World.content:
Romanian swimming star David Popovici has won the 200m freestyle race at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, his third consecutive European title in the event.

The win on August 14, following the August 12 gold in the 100m freestyle race, makes him the only athlete to have won both races at three consecutive editions of the European championships.

The 21-year-old Romanian swimmer finished the race with a time of 1:44.15, 0.40 seconds ahead of runner-up Tomas Navikonis of Lithuania, and 0.72 seconds ahead of Britain's James Guy.

In the 200m freestyle event, Popovici also won the Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, as well as two world titles, in Budapest in 2022 and in Singapore in 2025.

His personal best in the 200m freestyle came at the 2022 European Championships, when he clocked 1:42.97, the third-fastest time in history.

World.title: Romanian executive to submit fifth payment request under Recovery and Resilience Facility
World.content:
The Romanian government is set to submit the fifth payment request under the EU-backed Recovery and Resilience Facility, or PNRR, according to an announcement from European Investments and Projects minister Dragoș Pîslaru.

Payment no. 5 is worth EUR 2.84 billion, and is the penultimate request that Romania will submit within the PNRR. Once approved, the fifth payment will bring Romania’s absorption rate of PNRR-related grants to 78%, from 66% currently.

“One final request remains, request no. 6, worth EUR 2.58 billion in grants and EUR 1.76 billion in loans. From a total of EUR 13.57 billion allocated at the time the PNRR was signed, we will reach EUR 10.56 billion after request no. 5,” Pîslaru said during a press conference.

Initially, the European Commission planned for a single final payment request, reuniting the now separated requests no. 5 and 6, the minister noted.

The final payment request will be submitted at the end of September, and with it “we could reach 97.2% of the PNRR,” he said, referring to the grants component.

“47% was the percentage of the PNRR when I came to the ministry, after four years since the program was launched. The annual average was about 10.4% of the PNRR. In one year and two months, under the Bolojan government, we added 31% of the PNRR,” the minister also said.

Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan is financed through EUR 21.41 billion under the EU mechanism, including EUR 13.57 billion in grants and EUR 7.84 billion in loans. The fourth payment request, worth EUR 2.62 billion, was approved by the European Commission in May of this year.

World.title: Drone crashes in Romania’s Tulcea County
World.content:
A drone crashed on Friday, August 14, in the area of Luncaviţa, a locality in eastern Romania’s Tulcea County, about five kilometers from the border with Ukraine, the Defense Ministry (MApN) announced.

The drone crashed in a wooded area and caused no casualties, according to preliminary information provided by MApN.

The drone was not detected by MApN’s radar surveillance systems as it was flying at a very low altitude, the ministry said.

The crash resulted in an explosion followed by a fire, which has been extinguished, the Emergency Situations Inspectorate of Tulcea announced.

A MApN team, using an IAR 330 PUMA SOCAT helicopter, will investigate the area.

A day earlier, drone remains were discovered in the sea, close to Romania’s Costinești beach, on the Black Sea shore. Five drones were tracked nearing Romanian territory on the night of Wednesday, August 12, to Thursday, August 13, around 1 AM. One drone briefly entered Romanian airspace in Tulcea County but then exited and headed to Ukraine. Another drone was detected in Romanian airspace around 9 AM. Earlier this week, two Gerbera-type drones were destroyed by divers of the Romanian Army in the exclusive economic zone, approximately 165 kilometers from Constanța, in the Neptun Deep exploitation area.

At the end of the August 14 government meeting, prime minister Ilie Bolojan said the country’s military was doing “everything in their power to combat the drones.”

“We have a reality that we cannot deny, namely that the war resulting from Russia’s aggression against Ukraine is having an impact, including along our borders, and we can expect drone debris, drones reaching the river areas along Romania’s border, in the vicinity of ports, to stray into Romania,” the PM said.

“It is regrettable that we are facing such situations, but given what has happened in recent months, we are beginning to see that this is becoming something of a constant; it is not just in Romania, we have seen what has happened in other areas as well. It is becoming clear that equipping our Armed Forces as quickly as possible with counter-drone systems is a necessity,” he added.

World.title: Romanian telco Digi reports 10% higher revenues in Q2 2026
World.content:
Romanian telecommunications company Digi (BVB: DIGI) reported consolidated revenues of EUR 608 million in the second quarter of 2026, representing an 11% YoY increase.

Adjusted EBITDA (ex. operating leases) for Q2 2026 increased by 23% compared to the result from Q2 2025, reaching EUR 169 million. Consequently, in the first semester of 2026, the group recorded consolidated revenues of EUR 1.2 billion, a 10% increase versus 6M 2025, and adjusted EBITDA of EUR 398 million, up 17% YoY.

“Spain continues to be our primary growth engine, maintaining strong commercial momentum and progressing in line with our long-term plans, while Romania continued to perform well,” said Serghei Bulgac, CEO of Digi Communications.

Last month, Digi successfully completed an initial public offering for its Spanish subsidiary. The Spanish IPO was multiple times oversubscribed, showing investor appetite for the company’s shares.

In Q2 2026, Digi reached 33.9 million revenue-generating user agreements (RGUs) across Romania, Spain, Portugal and Italy, a 14% increase compared to Q2 2025.

The mobile segment stands out for generating the most RGUs within the group’s array of services, accounting for 51% of the overall clients across the four markets. In Q2 2026, the mobile segment saw its RGUs climb to 17.3 million, a 19% YoY increase, covering mobile telephony clients across Romania, Spain, Portugal and Italy.

In Romania, the mobile service segment remained the largest, reaching 8.4 million RGUs as of the end of Q2 2026, a positive evolution of 20% compared to Q2 2025. Broadband services registered an increase of 4% in Q2 2026, compared to Q2 2025, up to 5.2 million RGUs, while the segment of Pay-TV services (cable and satellite) increased by 2% YoY, up to 6.1 million RGUs. Together with fixed-line telephony, the total number of RGUs in the Romanian market amounted to 20.5 million customers as of Q2 2026, a 9% increase versus Q2 2025.

Spanish operations continued the strong performance in Q2 2026, with the number of users of fixed services, internet, and mobile telephony increasing by 23% compared to Q2 2025, to 11.9 million RGUs. Mobile users increased by 19% to 7.8 million RGUs, while broadband users increased by 28% to 2.9 million.

In Portugal, the number of RGUs amounted to 960k, up 22% YoY, of which 545k were mobile, and 186k were broadband users.

In Italy, mobile users increased by 4,5% YoY, reaching 535k RGUs as of the end of Q2 2026.

In the United Kingdom, Digi launched its fiber broadband services and continued expanding its network footprint during the second quarter of 2026, while onboarding its first customers.

World.title: Romania’s Presidential Administration to host summit on animal welfare
World.content:
The Presidential Administration will host the second edition of Animal Summit Romania on September 29 - 30, Diana Pungă, a state adviser for relations with civil society at the institution, announced on Friday, August 14.

The event, organized by the non-profit Sache Vet Association and Bucharest’s Animal Protection Administration ASPA, will take place at Cotroceni Palace.

Over two days, it will gather public administration representatives, veterinarians, legal and education specialists, non-governmental organizations and other experts to discuss animal protection and welfare and solutions to challenges in the field.

“Romania continues to face major challenges in the field of animal protection. Beyond the issue of abandonment and the lack of education about responsible pet ownership, civil society frequently raises concerns about the non-transparent operation of some private shelters, suspected abusive euthanasia practices and difficulties in uniformly enforcing existing legislation. In many communities, volunteers, NGOs and active citizens end up compensating for the lack of coherent institutional mechanisms by becoming directly involved in animal rescue, shelter monitoring and the promotion of responsible sterilization and adoption,” an announcement from the organizers reads.

All of these aspects point to an urgent need for clear standards and consistently implemented public policies protecting both the communities and the animals, the organizers said.

World.title: Central Romania: EBRD extends EUR 120 mln loan for PV plant, battery system near Brașov
World.content:
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) announced on Friday, August 14, that it has extended a financing package of up to EUR 120 million for the development, construction, and operation of Econergy’s Părău 2 project in Romania.

The project includes a 342 MW solar photovoltaic plant and a 150 MW/300 MWh battery storage system in Brașov, according to a statement by the lender.

The financing consists of an EBRD A loan of up to EUR 57 million and an EBRD B loan of up to EUR 63 million, which includes a EUR 3.6 million debt service guarantee provided by commercial banks Privredna banka Zagreb and NLB.

According to the EBRD, the Părău 2 project will increase renewable energy production, help improve grid flexibility, and strengthen Romania’s energy security.

The project is co-financed by BSTDB (the Black Sea Trade and Development Bank), OTP Bank, and Exim Banca Românească, as part of a debt financing package of up to EUR 229 million.

“By financing one of the country’s pioneering solar and battery storage investments, the EBRD is helping to increase the generation of renewable energy, strengthen energy security and support a more resilient and flexible electricity system. The support of the European Union through InvestEU demonstrates how public and private partners can work together to mobilize financing for the green transition,” said Georgios Gkiaouris, the EBRD’s Head of Energy Europe.

The project is backed by Romania’s Contract for Difference scheme, which was developed with EBRD technical assistance and aims to unlock 5 GW of solar and onshore wind capacity. The solar plant has secured a 125 MWac allocation in the first auction at a strike price of EUR 49.4/MWh for 15 years, while the remaining capacity will operate on a merchant basis.

The European Union supported the EBRD A/B loan through a first-loss portfolio guarantee provided by the InvestEU programme, which covers up to EUR 115 million and helps mitigate the risks associated with the project’s substantial exposure to merchant revenue.

World.title: Romanian consumer goods distributor AQUILA reports slightly higher revenues amid challenging context
World.content:
AQUILA, one of the largest players in the fast-moving consumer goods distribution sector from Romania and the region, reported revenues of RON 1.6 billion in the first half of 2026, amid an economic environment marked by declining consumption, according to a report submitted to the local stock exchange.

The figure represents a 6.4% increase compared to the same period last year.

Revenue from the distribution segment increased by 6% in the first half of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, driven by the organic growth of this business line. The main contributor to this performance was the traditional retail channel, which grew by 22%, followed by the HoReCa channel with 7% growth, and the gas station channel with 1%, evolutions that offset the 19% decline recorded in the organized retail channel.

Revenue from the logistics segment increased by 6%, driven by higher operating volumes and the expansion of logistics activities across multiple temperature categories, particularly in the frozen products segment. Revenue from the transport segment increased by 13%.

The company's own brands continued to strengthen their contribution to the group’s performance, with revenues of RON 78.5 million in the first half of 2026, up 23% compared to the same period in 2025.

The results for the first half of the year were affected by a more challenging operating environment, marked by weaker consumer spending in Romania, an approximately 30% increase in fuel costs, and unfavorable foreign exchange movements, as well as by the temporary impact of the group’s market share expansion strategy and continued investments in the development of our operating platform.

In this context, EBITDA amounted to approximately RON 61 million, down 33% compared to the same period in 2025, while the net result was negative, at approximately RON 21 million.

During the first six months of the year, the group invested EUR 3 million in the development of its logistics infrastructure, process digitalization, operations automation, and equipment modernization, in line with its growth strategy and commitment to improving operational efficiency.

“Our distribution segment continued to deliver growth, supported by the expansion of the traditional retail and HoReCa channels, the consolidated contribution of our own brands, and the commercial synergies generated through the integration of the acquired companies. At the same time, we chose to prioritize strengthening commercial relationships and increasing market share, which play an essential role in supporting long-term growth and value creation,” said Cătălin Vasile, CEO of AQUILA.

The company head noted that the strategy had a temporary impact on commercial margins and profitability but created “a foundation for capitalizing on the investments made and supporting sustainable performance in the period ahead.”
